title.raw: 卷74 尒朱榮 Volume 74: Er Zhurong

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮

translations.literal: Er Zhurong
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮，字天寶，北秀容人也。

translations.literal: Er Zhurong, courtesy name Tianbao, was a native of Northern Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong, styled Tianbao, came from Northern Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 其先居於尒朱川，因為氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt on the Erzhu River, and thereby took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had lived on the Erzhu River and took that place as their surname.

sentences.zh: 常領部落，世為酋帥。

translations.literal: They constantly led the tribal group and for generations served as chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they led their tribe as hereditary chieftains.

sentences.zh: 高祖羽健，登國初為領民酋長，率契胡武士千七百人從駕平晉陽，定中山。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Yu Jian, at the beginning of the Dengguo era, served as Leader of the Tribal People, leading seventeen hundred Qihu warriors in the imperial retinue to pacify Jinyang and settle Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yu Jian, in the early years of the state, served as chieftain over the tribal peoples and led seventeen hundred Qihu warriors in the emperor's train to pacify Jinyang and secure Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 論功拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In recognition of his merit he was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以居秀容川，詔割方三百里封之，長為世業。

translations.literal: Because he dwelt at Xiurong River, an edict carved out three hundred li square and enfeoffed him with it, to be his family's permanent holding.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family lived on the Xiurong River, the throne granted them a domain three hundred li on a side, held in perpetuity as their hereditary estate.

sentences.zh: 太祖初以南秀容川原沃衍，欲令居之，羽健曰：「臣家世奉國，給侍左右。

translations.literal: In the early days of Emperor Taizu, because the plains of Southern Xiurong River were fertile and expansive, he wished to have them relocate there. Yu Jian said: "My family for generations has served the state, attending at Your Majesty's side.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taizu's reign, the emperor noted that the Southern Xiurong River valley was rich and broad and wished to move the clan there. Yu Jian replied: "My family has served the dynasty for generations, always at the sovereign's side.

sentences.zh: 北秀容既在剗內，差近京師，豈以沃塉更遷遠地。」

translations.literal: Northern Xiurong is already within the barrier lands and somewhat close to the capital — how could we, for richer soil, relocate to a more distant place?"
translations.idiomatic: Northern Xiurong already lies within the frontier belt and is reasonably close to the capital. How could we abandon it for richer ground farther away?"

sentences.zh: 太祖許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 所居之處，曾有狗舐地，因而穿之，得甘泉焉，至今名狗舐泉。

translations.literal: At the place where they lived, a dog once licked the ground; when they dug there they found a sweet spring, which to this day is called Dog-Licking Spring.
translations.idiomatic: At their settlement a dog once licked the earth; when men dug there they found a sweet spring, still known today as Dog-Licking Spring.

sentences.zh: 羽健，世祖時卒。

translations.literal: Yu Jian died during the reign of Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian died in the reign of Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖鬱德，祖代勤，繼為領民酋長。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Yude; his grandfather Daiqin; both in succession served as Leaders of the Tribal People.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yude and his grandfather Daiqin each succeeded to the post of chieftain over the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 代勤，世祖敬哀皇后之舅。

translations.literal: Daiqin was maternal uncle to Emperor Shizu's Empress Jing'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Daiqin was the maternal uncle of Emperor Shizu's Empress Jing'ai.

sentences.zh: 以外親兼數征伐有功，給復百年，除立義將軍。

translations.literal: As a relative by marriage who also rendered merit in several campaigns, he was granted exemption from taxes for a hundred years and appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: As an imperial in-law who also won distinction in several campaigns, he was granted a century of tax remission and appointed General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 曾圍山而獵，部民射虎，誤中其髀，代勤仍令拔箭，竟不推問，曰：「此既過誤，何忍加罪。」

translations.literal: Once while hunting with a mountain enclosure, a tribesman shooting at a tiger accidentally struck him in the thigh. Daiqin still had him pull out the arrow and never pursued an investigation, saying: "This was already an accident — how could I bear to punish him?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while hunting within a mountain enclosure, a tribesman firing at a tiger accidentally struck him in the thigh. Daiqin had the arrow drawn out and never pressed the matter, saying: "This was plainly a mistake — how could I punish him for it?"

sentences.zh: 部內聞之，咸感其意。

translations.literal: When those within his jurisdiction heard of it, all were moved by his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of it within his domain were moved by his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，假寧南將軍，除肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, he was provisionally made General Who Pacifies the South and appointed Prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Gaozong's reign he was made acting General Who Pacifies the South and appointed prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜爵梁郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu bestowed on him the title Duke of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ennobled him as Duke of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以老致仕，歲賜帛百匹以為常。

translations.literal: He retired on account of age, and was granted a hundred bolts of silk annually as a fixed stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He retired for old age and received a standing grant of a hundred bolts of silk each year.

sentences.zh: 年九十一，卒。

translations.literal: At age ninety-one he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-one.

sentences.zh: 賜帛五百匹、布二百匹，贈鎮南將軍、并州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred bolts of silk and two hundred of cloth; posthumously awarded General Who Guards the South and Prefect of Bingzhou, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted five hundred bolts of silk and two hundred of cloth, and posthumously honored him as General Who Guards the South and prefect of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，榮有翼戴之勳，追贈太師、司徒公、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, because Zhurong had merit in supporting and elevating the throne, Daiqin was posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Manager of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang first took the throne, Zhurong's service in raising him to power was remembered, and Daiqin was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Manager of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父新興，太和中，繼為酋長。

translations.literal: His father Xinxing, during the Taihe era, succeeded as chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinxing succeeded as chieftain during the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 家世豪擅，財貨豐贏。

translations.literal: The family for generations was powerful and dominant, with abundant wealth and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The clan had long been powerful and wealthy, its stores of goods overflowing.

sentences.zh: 曾行馬羣，見一白蛇，頭有兩角，遊於馬前。

translations.literal: Once while driving a herd of horses, he saw a white serpent with two horns on its head roaming before the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while moving a herd of horses, he saw a white serpent with two horns on its head glide before the mounts.

sentences.zh: 新興異之，謂曰：「爾若有神，令我畜牧蕃息。」

translations.literal: Xinxing marveled at it and said: "If you have divine power, cause my herds to multiply and flourish."
translations.idiomatic: Xinxing was astonished and addressed it: "If you are divine, let my herds multiply and thrive."

sentences.zh: 自是之後，日覺滋盛，牛羊駝馬，色別為羣，谷量而已。

translations.literal: From that time on, day by day they seemed to grow ever more abundant; cattle, sheep, camels, and horses were sorted by color into separate herds, measured only by the granary-load.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the herds grew richer day by day; cattle, sheep, camels, and horses were grouped by color into separate droves, counted only by the granary-load.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有征討，輒獻私馬，兼備資糧，助裨軍用。

translations.literal: Whenever the court undertook campaigns, he would present his private horses and also supply provisions to assist the military effort.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court mounted a campaign, he offered his own horses and furnished provisions to bolster the army.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，除右將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu commended him and appointed him General of the Right and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised him and appointed him General of the Right and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛後，特聽冬朝京師，夏歸部落。

translations.literal: After the transfer of the capital to Luoyang, he was specially permitted to attend court in the capital in winter and return to his tribe in summer.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, he was specially allowed to attend court in the capital in winter and return to his tribe in summer.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，諸王公朝貴競以珍玩遺之，新興亦報以名馬。

translations.literal: Each time he came to court, the princes and nobles vied to send him rare curios, and Xinxing reciprocated with famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court, princes and court grandees competed to send him rare treasures, and Xinxing repaid them with fine horses.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍、平北將軍、秀容第一領民酋長。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and First Leader of the Tribal People of Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and First Chieftain of the Tribal Peoples of Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 新興每春秋二時，恒與妻子閱畜牧於川澤，射獵自娛。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn Xinxing would regularly review the herds with his wife and children in the rivers and marshes, hunting for his own amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn Xinxing would take his wife and children to inspect the herds in the rivers and marshes and hunt for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 肅宗世，以年老啟求傳爵於榮，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: During Emperor Suzong's reign, citing old age he petitioned to pass his title to Zhurong, and the court permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzong's reign, citing his age, he petitioned to pass his title to Zhurong, and the court granted the request.

sentences.zh: 正光中卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhengguang era, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhengguang era, at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、平北將軍、恒州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Prefect of Hengzhou, with the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and prefect of Hengzhou, with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，贈假黃鉞、侍中、太師、相國、西河郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and King of Xihe Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhuang first took the throne, Xinxing was posthumously granted the ceremonial axe, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Chancellor of State, and the title King of Xihe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 榮潔白，美容貌，幼而神機明決。

translations.literal: Zhurong was fair-skinned and handsome; even as a child he showed keen spirit and clear decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhurong was fair-complexioned and handsome; even as a boy he showed sharp insight and resolute judgment.

sentences.zh: 及長，好射獵，每設圍誓眾，便為軍陳之法，號令嚴肅，眾莫敢犯。

translations.literal: When grown, he loved hunting; whenever he set up an encirclement hunt and rallied the crowd, he would arrange them in battle formation, his orders stern and solemn — none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he loved the hunt; whenever he organized a drive and mustered the men, he drilled them in battle formation with stern commands, and none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 秀容界有池三所，在高山之上，清深不測，相傳曰祁連池，魏言天池也。

translations.literal: Within Xiurong territory there were three pools atop high mountains, clear and fathomless; by tradition they were called Qilian Pools, which in Wei speech meant Heavenly Pools.
translations.idiomatic: Within Xiurong lay three pools on high mountains, clear and unfathomably deep; tradition called them the Qilian Pools, which in the Wei tongue meant Heavenly Pools.

sentences.zh: 父新興，曾與榮遊池上，忽聞簫鼓之音。

translations.literal: His father Xinxing once went to the pools with Zhurong and suddenly heard the sound of panpipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinxing once visited the pools with Zhurong and suddenly heard the sound of flutes and drums.

sentences.zh: 新興謂榮曰：「古老相傳，凡聞此聲皆至公輔。

translations.literal: Xinxing said to Zhurong: "The ancients handed down that whoever hears this sound will rise to the highest ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xinxing told Zhurong: "The old tradition holds that whoever hears this sound will reach the highest offices of state.

sentences.zh: 吾今年已衰暮，當為汝耳。

translations.literal: I am already in my declining years — it will be yours.
translations.idiomatic: I am already in my decline; the omen is meant for you.

sentences.zh: 汝其勉之。」

translations.literal: Strive your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: You must apply yourself."

sentences.zh: 榮襲爵後，除直寢、游擊將軍。

translations.literal: After Zhurong inherited the title, he was appointed Direct Attendant and General of Mobile Striking Forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhurong succeeded to the title, he was appointed Direct Attendant and General of Mobile Striking Forces.

sentences.zh: 正光中，四方兵起，遂散畜牧，招合義勇，給其衣馬。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era, as warfare erupted on all sides, he dispersed his herds, gathered voluntary fighters, and supplied them with clothing and horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era, when war broke out on every side, he broke up his herds, gathered volunteers, and clothed and mounted them.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕主阿那瓌寇掠北鄙，詔假榮節，冠軍將軍、別將，隸都督李崇北征。

translations.literal: When the Rouran ruler Anagui raided the northern frontier, an edict provisionally granted Zhurong insignia of authority as General Who Conquers the Champions and a separate commander, subordinate to the Grand Commander Li Chong on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran khan Anagui raided the northern border, the throne granted Zhurong command authority as General Who Conquers the Champions and a detached commander under the grand commander Li Chong on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 榮率其新部四千人追擊，度磧，不及而還。

translations.literal: Zhurong led his newly mustered force of four thousand in pursuit, crossed the desert, failed to overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhurong led his newly raised force of four thousand in pursuit, crossed the desert, failed to catch the enemy, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 秀容內附胡民乞扶莫于破郡，殺太守；

translations.literal: Within Xiurong, the attached Hu tribesman Qifumoyu broke through the commandery and killed the prefect;
translations.idiomatic: In Xiurong the attached Hu tribesman Qifumoyu stormed the commandery seat and killed the prefect;

sentences.zh: 南秀容牧子萬子乞真反叛，[1]殺太僕卿陸延；

translations.literal: the herder Wanzhiqizhen of Southern Xiurong rebelled [1] and killed the Minister of the Imperial Stud Lu Yan;
translations.idiomatic: the herder Wanzhiqizhen of Southern Xiurong rebelled [1] and killed the Minister of the Imperial Stud Lu Yan;

sentences.zh: 并州牧子素和婆崘嶮作逆。

translations.literal: the herder Suhepola of Bingzhou rose in revolt on difficult terrain.
translations.idiomatic: and the herder Suhepola of Bingzhou rose in rebellion from a mountain stronghold.

sentences.zh: 榮並前後討平之。

translations.literal: Zhurong in succession suppressed and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhurong put them all down in turn.

sentences.zh: 遷直閤將軍、冠軍將軍，仍別將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Direct Gate and General Who Conquers the Champions, still serving as a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Direct Gate and General Who Conquers the Champions, continuing as a detached commander.

sentences.zh: 內附叛胡乞、步落堅胡劉阿如等作亂瓜肆，[2]敕勒北列步若反於沃陽，[3]榮並滅之。

translations.literal: Attached rebel Hu such as Qi and the Buluoqiian Hu Liu Aru stirred up trouble in Guasi [2]; the Tiele Buluobu rebelled at Woyang [3] — Zhurong destroyed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Attached rebel Hu such as Qi and the Buluoqiian Hu Liu Aru raised disturbances in Guasi [2]; the Tiele Buluobu rebelled at Woyang [3] — Zhurong destroyed them all.

sentences.zh: 以功封安平縣開國侯，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis Who Establishes the State of Anping County, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Marquis Who Establishes the State of Anping County, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was additionally made Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission in Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made Regular Attendant of Direct Transmission in Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 敕勒斛律洛陽作逆桑乾西，[4]與費也頭牧子迭相掎角，榮率騎破洛陽於深井，逐牧子於河西。

translations.literal: The Tiele Hulu Luoyang rebelled west of the Sanggan [4]; together with the Paytou herders they alternately supported each other in pincer fashion. Zhurong led cavalry to defeat Luoyang at Shenjing and drove the herders west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele chieftain Hulu Luoyang rebelled west of the Sanggan [4]; he and the Paytou herders supported one another in alternating pincers. Zhurong led cavalry to defeat Luoyang at Shenjing and drove the herders west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 進號平北將軍、光祿大夫，假安北將軍，為北道都督。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; provisionally General Who Pacifies the North; he served as Grand Commander of the Northern Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, made acting General Who Pacifies the North, and appointed grand commander of the northern route.

sentences.zh: 尋除武衞將軍，俄加使持節、安北將軍、都督恒朔討虜諸軍、假撫軍將軍，進封博陵郡公，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was appointed General of Martial Guard; soon granted the credential staff, made General Who Pacifies the North, Grand Commander of all armies for suppressing barbarians in Heng and Shuozhou, provisionally General Who Pacifies the Army; advanced to Duke of Boling Commandery with an additional fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made General of Martial Guard; shortly thereafter he received the credential staff as General Who Pacifies the North and grand commander of all armies for suppressing the barbarians of Heng and Shuozhou, with acting rank as General Who Pacifies the Army; he was advanced to Duke of Boling Commandery with an additional fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其梁郡前爵，聽賜第二子。

translations.literal: His prior title of Liang Commandery was permitted to be granted to his second son.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier title of Liang Commandery was permitted to pass to his second son.

sentences.zh: 時榮率眾至肆州，刺史尉慶賓畏惡之，閉城不納。

translations.literal: At that time Zhurong led his troops to Sizhou; the prefect Wei Qingbin feared and detested him and shut the city gates, refusing entry.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhurong led his troops to Sizhou; the prefect Wei Qingbin feared and hated him and shut the gates, refusing him entry.

sentences.zh: 榮怒，攻拔之，乃署其從叔羽生為刺史，執慶賓於秀容。

translations.literal: Zhurong in anger stormed and took it, then installed his father's cousin Yusheng as prefect and held Qingbin captive at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Zhurong stormed and captured the city, installed his father's cousin Yusheng as prefect, and held Qingbin prisoner at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 自是榮兵威漸盛，朝廷亦不能罪責也。

translations.literal: From this time Zhurong's military prestige gradually grew, and the court could no longer hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zhurong's military power steadily grew, and the court could no longer punish him.

sentences.zh: 尋除鎮北將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was appointed General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 鮮于脩禮之反也，榮表東討，復進號征東將軍、右衞將軍、假車騎將軍、都督并肆汾廣恒雲六州諸軍事，進為大都督，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled, Zhurong memorialized requesting an eastern campaign; his titles were again advanced to General Who Conquers the East, General of the Right Guard, provisionally General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Commander of all military affairs in the six provinces of Bing, Si, Fen, Guang, Heng, and Yun; promoted to Grand Commander-in-Chief; additionally made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled, Zhurong memorialized asking to campaign east; he was again promoted to General Who Conquers the East, General of the Right Guard, and acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, with grand command over military affairs in the six provinces of Bing, Si, Fen, Guang, Heng, and Yun; he was raised to grand commander-in-chief and given the rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 時杜洛周陷中山，於時車駕聲將北討，以榮為左軍，不行。

translations.literal: At that time Du Luozhou had taken Zhongshan; the imperial carriage was rumored to be setting out on a northern campaign with Zhurong as the Left Army — but this did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Luozhou had captured Zhongshan; rumor had it that the emperor would lead a northern campaign with Zhurong as the left wing, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮吞洛周，凶勢轉盛。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong swallowed up Luozhou, his violent power grew still stronger.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou's forces, his ferocious power grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 榮恐其南逼鄴城，表求遣騎三千東援相州，肅宗不許。

translations.literal: Zhurong feared they would press south toward Ye City and memorialized requesting three thousand cavalry sent east to aid Xiangzhou; Emperor Suzong did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhurong feared they would press south toward Ye and memorialized asking to send three thousand cavalry east to relieve Xiangzhou; Suzong refused.

sentences.zh: 又遷車騎將軍、右光祿大夫，尋進位儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; shortly after advanced to the Three Ducal Equivalents.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and soon afterward advanced to the Three Ducal Equivalents.

sentences.zh: 榮以山東賊盛，慮其西逸，乃遣兵固守滏口以防之。

translations.literal: Zhurong, because rebels in Shandong were strong and he feared they would break westward, dispatched troops to hold Fokou firmly in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebels in Shandong were strong and he feared they might break westward, Zhurong sent troops to hold Fokou and block them.

sentences.zh: 復上書曰：「臣前以二州頻反，大軍喪敗，河北無援，實慮南侵，故令精騎三千出援相州，京師影響，斷其南望，賊聞此眾，當亦息圖。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant previously, because the two provinces rebelled repeatedly and the main army suffered defeat, with Hebei lacking reinforcements and truly fearing southern invasion, therefore ordered three thousand elite cavalry to go out and aid Xiangzhou, so that the capital would cast its shadow of influence and cut off their southern ambitions — when the rebels hear of such a force, they should likewise abandon their designs.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "Your servant previously, seeing the two provinces rebel again and again and the main army defeated, with Hebei left without relief and real fear of a southern thrust, ordered three thousand elite cavalry to aid Xiangzhou so that the capital's prestige would reach that far, cutting off the rebels' hopes of moving south. When they heard of such a force, they would surely abandon their plans.

sentences.zh: 使還，奉敕云：『念生梟勠，寶夤受擒，醜奴、明達並送誠款，三輔告謐，關隴載寧。

translations.literal: The envoy returned with an edict stating: 'Niansheng was executed, Mo Bao was captured, Chou and Mingda both sent pledges of submission — the Three Metropolises report peace, and Guan and Long are again tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned bearing an edict: 'Niansheng has been executed, Mo Bao captured, Chou and Mingda have both submitted in good faith; the Three Metropolises report calm, and Guan and Long are at peace again.

sentences.zh: 費穆虎旅，大翦妖蠻；

translations.literal: Fei Mu's tiger brigades have greatly clipped the demonic barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu's tiger brigades have cut down the demonic barbarians in force;

sentences.zh: 兩絳狂蜀，漸已稽顙。』

translations.literal: the raging Shu of the two Jiangs have gradually begun to bow their foreheads.'
translations.idiomatic: the raging Shu rebels of the two Jiang regions are already beginning to bow their heads.'

sentences.zh: 又承北海王顥率眾二萬出鎮相州。

translations.literal: It was further reported that Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was leading twenty thousand men to go out and garrison Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It was also reported that Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was leading twenty thousand men to take up command at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 北海皇孫，名位崇重，鎮撫鄴城，實副羣望。

translations.literal: The Beihai prince, an imperial grandson, is lofty in name and station; to pacify Ye City fulfills the hopes of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beihai is an imperial grandson of high name and rank; to place him in command at Ye answers the hopes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 惟願廣其配衣，及機早遣。

translations.literal: I only wish his supplementary guards and retinue be expanded, and that he be dispatched at the earliest opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: I only ask that his guard and retinue be enlarged and that he be sent out at once.

sentences.zh: 今關西雖平，兵未可役，山南隣賊，理無發召，王師雖眾，頻被摧北，人情危怯，實謂難用，若不更思方略，無以萬全。

translations.literal: Now though Guanxi is pacified, troops cannot yet be deployed; with neighboring rebels to the south of the mountains, there is no reason to summon them — though the imperial army is numerous, it has repeatedly been shattered northward; men's hearts are fearful and timid and truly difficult to employ; if no new strategy is devised, there will be no way to secure complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: Though Guanxi is now pacified, those troops cannot yet be used; with neighboring rebels south of the mountains, there is no reason to summon them. Though the imperial army is large, it has repeatedly been broken in the north, and men's hearts are fearful and timid — truly hard troops to use. Unless a new strategy is devised, there is no way to secure complete safety.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚量，蠕蠕主阿那瓌荷國厚恩，未應忘報，求乞一使慰喻那瓌。

translations.literal: By your servant's feeble reckoning, the Rouran ruler Anagui has received the state's deep kindness and ought not forget repayment — I beg to send one envoy to comfort and instruct Anagui.
translations.idiomatic: By your servant's poor judgment, the Rouran khan Anagui has received the state's deep kindness and ought not to forget his debt — I beg that one envoy be sent to reassure and instruct him.

sentences.zh: 即遣發兵東引，直趣下口，揚威振武，以躡其背；

translations.literal: Have him promptly dispatch troops eastward, pressing straight toward Xiakou, displaying power and shaking might, to press on their rear;
translations.idiomatic: Then have him send troops east at once, pressing straight toward Xiakou, displaying power and striking terror, to fall upon the enemy's rear;

sentences.zh: 北海之軍，鎮撫相部，嚴加警備，以當其前；

translations.literal: the Beihai army to pacify and settle the Xiang region, with strict watch and defense to meet them at the front;
translations.idiomatic: the Beihai army to pacify and hold the Xiang region, with strict watch and defense to meet them head-on;

sentences.zh: 臣麾下雖少，輒盡力命，自井陘以北，隘口以西，分防險要，攻其肘腋。

translations.literal: though your servant's forces below are few, I will exhaust my strength and life, from north of Jingxing to west of the passes, dividing defense of strategic points and striking their flanks.
translations.idiomatic: though your servant's own forces are few, I will spend my last strength holding the strategic points from north of Jingxing to west of the passes, and strike their flanks.

sentences.zh: 葛榮雖并洛周，威恩未著，人類差異，形勢可分。」

translations.literal: Ge Rong though he has absorbed Luozhou, his prestige and grace are not yet established; the peoples differ; the situation can be split."
translations.idiomatic: Though Ge Rong has absorbed Luozhou, his authority and favor are not yet secure; the peoples under him differ, and the situation can still be divided."

sentences.zh: 於是榮遂嚴勒部曲，廣召義勇，北捍馬邑，東塞井陘。

translations.literal: With this, Zhurong thereupon tightened discipline over his troops, widely summoned volunteers, defended Mayi to the north, and blocked Jingxing to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhurong tightened discipline among his troops, widely summoned volunteers, defended Mayi to the north, and blocked Jingxing to the east.

sentences.zh: 尋屬肅宗崩，事出倉卒，榮聞之大怒，謂鄭儼、徐紇為之，與元天穆等密議稱兵入匡朝廷，討定之。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Emperor Suzong died — a matter arising in sudden haste. When Zhurong heard of it he was greatly enraged, believing Zheng Yan and Xu He had done it; with Yuan Tianmu and others he secretly deliberated raising troops to enter and rectify the court, punishing and settling the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Suzong died — a sudden, unforeseen event. When Zhurong heard the news he was furious, believing Zheng Yan and Xu He responsible; with Yuan Tianmu and others he secretly planned to raise troops, enter the capital, set the court right, and punish those responsible.

sentences.zh: 乃抗表曰：「伏承大行皇帝背棄萬方，奉諱號踴，五內摧剝。

translations.literal: He then submitted a defiant memorial stating: "I humbly receive word that the late emperor has abandoned the myriad realms; receiving the mournful tidings I am convulsed with grief, my five viscera torn and shredded.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a defiant memorial: "I humbly learn that the late emperor has left the myriad realms; upon receiving the mournful tidings I am convulsed with grief, my innermost being torn apart.

sentences.zh: 仰尋詔旨，實用驚惋。

translations.literal: Looking up to examine the edict's purport, I am truly shocked and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the edict's purport, I am truly shocked and dismayed.

sentences.zh: 今海內草草，異口一言，皆云大行皇帝，鴆毒致禍。

translations.literal: Now throughout the realm there is uproar; with one voice all say the late emperor met disaster through poison.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is in uproar, and with one voice all say the late emperor met his end by poison.

sentences.zh: 臣等外聽訟言，內自追測。

translations.literal: We ministers without listen to public clamor; within we trace and investigate for ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers listen to the public outcry without, and within we trace and investigate for ourselves.

sentences.zh: 去月二十五日聖體康悆，至於二十六日奄忽昇遐。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth of last month the sacred person was hale and well; yet on the twenty-sixth he suddenly ascended to the far realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth of last month the emperor's person was still hale and well; yet on the twenty-sixth he suddenly departed this life.

sentences.zh: 即事觀望，實有所惑。

translations.literal: Observing the matter as it stands, I am truly perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the matter as it stands, I am truly perplexed.

sentences.zh: 且天子寢疾，侍臣不離左右，親貴名醫，瞻仰患狀，面奉音旨，親承顧託。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Son of Heaven was ill in bed, attendants never left his side; noble physicians of repute observed the symptoms face to face, received his verbal instructions, and personally accepted his final charge.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the Son of Heaven lay ill, attendants never left his side; eminent physicians observed his symptoms at close hand, received his words face to face, and personally accepted his final charge.

sentences.zh: 豈容不豫初不召醫，崩棄曾無親奉，欲使天下不為怪愕，四海不為喪氣，豈可得乎？

translations.literal: How could it be tolerated that at the first sign of illness no physician was summoned, and at death not a single intimate was present — yet one would have the realm not be shocked and astonished, the four seas not lose heart — is this possible?
translations.idiomatic: How could it be tolerated that at the first sign of illness no physician was summoned, and at death no intimate was present — yet one would have the realm neither shocked nor the four seas disheartened? Is such a thing possible?

sentences.zh: 復皇后女生，稱為儲兩，疑惑朝野，虛行慶宥，宗廟之靈見欺，兆民之望已失，使七百危於累卵，社禝墜於一朝，方選君嬰孩之中，寄治乳抱之日，使姦豎專朝，賊臣亂紀，惟欲指影以行權，假形而弄詔，此則掩眼捕雀，塞耳盜鍾。

translations.literal: Then the empress gave birth to a daughter, yet she was proclaimed heir — bewildering court and countryside, granting empty amnesties in celebration; the spirits of the ancestral temple are deceived, the hopes of the myriad people are lost, putting the seven hundred states in peril piled like eggs, the altars of soil and grain toppling in a single morning — choosing a ruler from among infants, entrusting governance to one still at the breast, letting wicked eunuchs monopolize the court and treacherous ministers overturn order, merely wishing to wield power by pointing at a shadow and manipulating edicts through a borrowed form — this is like covering the eyes to catch sparrows or stopping the ears to steal a bell.
translations.idiomatic: Then the empress bore a daughter, yet she was proclaimed heir — bewildering court and countryside, granting empty amnesties in celebration. The ancestral spirits are deceived, the people's hopes betrayed; the seven hundred states stand perilous as a pile of eggs, the altars of soil and grain ready to fall in a morning. A ruler is chosen from among infants, governance entrusted to one still at the breast, while wicked eunuchs monopolize the court and treacherous ministers overturn order, wielding power by pointing at a shadow and forging edicts through a borrowed form — this is covering the eyes to catch sparrows, stopping the ears to steal a bell.

sentences.zh: 今秦隴塵飛，趙魏霧合，寶夤、醜奴勢逼豳雍，葛榮、就德憑陵河海，楚兵吳卒密邇在郊。

translations.literal: Now dust flies in Qin and Long, mists gather in Zhao and Wei; Mo Bao and Chou press upon Bin and Yong; Ge Rong and Jiude encroach upon the rivers and seas; Chu soldiers and Wu troops press close upon the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Now dust rises in Qin and Long and mists gather over Zhao and Wei; Mo Bao and Chou threaten Bin and Yong; Ge Rong and Jiude menace the rivers and seas; Chu soldiers and Wu troops press close upon the capital's outskirts.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：邦之不臧，隣之福也。

translations.literal: The ancients have a saying: When a state is not good, it is the neighbor's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: When a state falls into disorder, its neighbors' fortune rises.

sentences.zh: 一旦聞此，誰不闚𨵦？

translations.literal: Once this is heard, who would not peer through the crevice in covetous watch?
translations.idiomatic: Once this is heard, who would not watch and covet an opening?

sentences.zh: 竊惟大行皇帝聖德馭宇，繼體正君，猶邊烽迭舉，妖寇不滅，況今從佞臣之計，隨親戚之談，舉潘嬪之女以誑百姓，奉未言之兒而臨四海，欲使海內安乂，愚臣所未聞也。

translations.literal: I privately consider that the late emperor, with sacred virtue governing the realm and succeeding legitimately to the throne, still saw frontier beacons rise again and again and demonic bandits undestroyed — how much less now, following the scheming of flatterers and the talk of kinsmen, raising the daughter of Lady Pan to deceive the common people and placing an infant who cannot yet speak over the four seas, yet wishing to make the realm within the seas peaceful and well-ordered — this your foolish servant has never heard of.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the late emperor, though he ruled with sacred virtue and succeeded legitimately to the throne, still saw frontier alarms rise again and again and demonic bandits go unextinguished — how much less can the realm be pacified now, when flatterers' schemes and kinsmen's counsel prevail, the daughter of Lady Pan is held up to deceive the people, and an infant who cannot yet speak is set over the four seas. Such a path to order within the seas your foolish servant has never heard of.

sentences.zh: 伏願留聖善之慈，回須臾之慮，照臣忠誠，錄臣至款，聽臣赴闕，預參大議，問侍臣帝崩之由，訪禁旅不知之狀，以徐、鄭之徒付之司敗，雪同天之耻，謝遠近之怨。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Majesty retain sacred kindness, turn back for a moment's consideration, recognize your servant's loyalty, record your servant's utmost sincerity, permit your servant to come to court, take part beforehand in the great deliberation, inquire of the attendants the cause of the emperor's death, investigate the condition of the palace guard who knew nothing of it, hand over Xu, Zheng, and their kind to the office of punishment, wipe away the shame equal to Heaven, and answer the grievances of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty retain your sacred kindness, turn back for a moment's thought, recognize my loyalty and accept my utmost sincerity, permit me to come to court and take part in the great deliberation, inquire of the attendants the cause of the emperor's death, investigate why the palace guard knew nothing of it, hand Xu, Zheng, and their kind over to justice, wipe away this shame that touches Heaven itself, and answer the grievances of near and far.

sentences.zh: 然後更召宗親，推其年德，聲副遐邇，改承寶祚，則四海更蘇，百姓幸甚。」

translations.literal: Then again summon the imperial kin, advance them by age and virtue, whose reputations match far and near, and have them succeed to the sacred throne — then the four seas would revive anew, and the common people would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Then summon the imperial kin once more, choose among them by age and virtue one whose name resounds far and near, and set him on the throne — the four seas would stir back to life, and the people would know great fortune.

sentences.zh: 於是遂勒所統將赴京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon he compelled the forces under his command and set out for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: With that he marched the troops under his command toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 靈太后甚懼，詔以李神軌為大都督，將於大行杜防。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was greatly afraid and issued an edict appointing Li Shengui as Grand Commander, with troops to block him on the great road.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was terrified. She issued an edict appointing Li Shengui Grand Commander and sent troops to bar his way on the main road.

sentences.zh: 十一日，榮奉帝為主，詔以榮為使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、大將軍、開府、兼尚書令、領軍將軍、領左右，太原王，食邑二萬戶。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day, Rong installed the emperor as ruler, and an edict appointed Rong Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Commissioner with an Open Office, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Central Army, Commander of the Left and Right Guard, Prince of Taiyuan, with a fief of twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day Er Zhurong raised the emperor to the throne. An edict named him Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Commissioner with an Open Office, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Central Army, Commander of the Left and Right Guard, Prince of Taiyuan, with a fief of twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 十二日，百官皆朝於行宮。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day, all officials attended court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day all officials attended court at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 十三日，榮惑武衞將軍費穆之說，乃引迎駕百官於行宮西北，云欲祭天。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day, Rong, swayed by the counsel of General of Martial Guard Fei Mu, led the officials who had come to welcome the imperial carriage to a spot northwest of the traveling palace, saying that he wished to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day, persuaded by General of Martial Guard Fei Mu, Rong summoned the officials who had come to welcome the emperor to a place northwest of the traveling palace, claiming he wished to perform a sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 朝士既集，列騎圍遶，責天下喪亂，明帝卒崩之由，云皆緣此等貪虐，不相匡弼所致。

translations.literal: Once the court gentlemen had assembled, cavalry drawn up in ranks encircled them. He charged them with the realm's disorder and the cause of Emperor Ming's sudden death, saying it all arose because such men were greedy and cruel and failed to support and correct one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the court officials had gathered, cavalry encircled them on every side. He denounced them for the chaos engulfing the realm and for Emperor Ming's sudden death, declaring that it all stemmed from their greed, cruelty, and failure to counsel and support the throne.

sentences.zh: 因縱兵亂害，王公卿士皆斂手就戮，死者千三百餘人，皇弟、皇兄並亦見害，靈太后、少主其日暴崩。

translations.literal: Thereupon he unleashed his troops in indiscriminate slaughter. Princes, dukes, ministers, and gentlemen all folded their hands and submitted to execution. More than thirteen hundred died. Imperial younger brothers and elder brothers were likewise killed. Empress Dowager Ling and the young ruler both died suddenly that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Then he loosed his troops in the Heyin massacre. Princes, ministers, and court officials folded their hands and went to the slaughter — more than thirteen hundred dead. Imperial brothers were killed as well. Empress Dowager Ling and the young emperor both perished violently that same day.

sentences.zh: 榮遂有大志，令御史趙元則造禪文，遣數十人遷帝於河橋。

translations.literal: Rong then conceived great ambitions. He ordered Censor Zhao Yuanze to draft an abdication text and sent several dozen men to move the emperor to He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's ambitions now swelled. He ordered Censor Zhao Yuanze to draft an abdication decree and sent several dozen men to escort the emperor to He Bridge.

sentences.zh: 至夜四更中，復奉帝南還營幕。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night he again escorted the emperor southward back to the camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth watch of the night he escorted the emperor south again to the camp.

sentences.zh: 帝憂憤無計，乃令人喻旨於榮曰：「帝王迭襲，盛衰無常，既屬屯運，四方瓦解。

translations.literal: The emperor, distressed and furious with no plan, had someone convey his meaning to Rong, saying: "Emperors succeed one another in turn; rise and decline have no fixed rule. Now that we have fallen into a time of hardship, the four quarters are collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: Anguished and desperate, the emperor sent a messenger to Rong with these words: "Emperors rise and fall in turn; fortune has no fixed course. Hard times have come, and the realm is crumbling on every side.

sentences.zh: 將軍杖義而起，前無橫陳，此乃天意，非人力也。

translations.literal: The general raised the banner of righteousness and none stood before you — this is Heaven's intent, not human effort.
translations.idiomatic: You raised the righteous standard and none could stand in your path — this is Heaven's will, not man's doing.

sentences.zh: 我本相投，規存性命，帝王重位，豈敢妄希，直是將軍見逼，權順所請耳。

translations.literal: I originally came to join you only to preserve my life. The weighty throne of emperor — how would I dare grasp at it recklessly? It was simply that the general pressed me, and I provisionally went along with your request.
translations.idiomatic: I came to you only to save my life. The imperial throne — how would I dare reach for it? You pressed me, and I merely yielded for the moment to your demand.

sentences.zh: 今璽運已移，天命有在，宜時即尊號。

translations.literal: Now the fortune of the seal has shifted; the Mandate of Heaven rests elsewhere. You should take the exalted title at once.
translations.idiomatic: The throne's fortune has passed from me; Heaven's mandate now rests with you. You should assume the imperial title without delay.

sentences.zh: 將軍必若推而不居，存魏社稷，亦任更擇親賢，共相輔戴。」

translations.literal: If the general insists on declining and not taking it, yet wishes to preserve the Wei state and altars, you may likewise choose anew from among the worthy kinsmen and jointly support and install one."
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse the throne yet mean to preserve Wei's altars, choose anew from among the worthy of the imperial clan and install one whom all can support together.

sentences.zh: 榮既有異圖，遂鑄金為己像，數四不成。

translations.literal: Rong, already harboring other designs, then cast gold into a statue of himself, but after several attempts it would not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong already nursed other ambitions. He had a gold statue of himself cast, but try as he might — four times — it would not take.

sentences.zh: 時幽州人劉靈助善卜占，為榮所信，言天時人事必不可爾。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Lingzhu of You Province was skilled in divination and was trusted by Rong. He said that by the signs of Heaven and affairs of men, it absolutely could not be so.
translations.idiomatic: A You Province man named Liu Lingzhu, skilled in divination and trusted by Rong, declared that Heaven and circumstance forbade it.

sentences.zh: 榮亦精神恍惚，不自支持，久而方悟，遂便愧悔。

translations.literal: Rong too became dazed in spirit, unable to sustain himself. Only after a long time did he come to his senses, and then he felt shame and remorse.
translations.idiomatic: Rong himself grew disoriented, barely able to stand. Long afterward he came to himself and was seized with shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 於是獻武王、榮外兵參軍司馬子如等切諫，陳不可之理。

translations.literal: Thereupon Prince Xianwu, Rong's external military adjutant Sima Ziru, and others urgently remonstrated, setting forth the reasons why it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu, Sima Ziru the external military adjutant, and others urgently remonstrated, explaining why he must not do it.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「愆誤若是，惟當以死謝朝廷，今日安危之機，計將何出？」

translations.literal: Rong said: "If my fault is so grave, I should repay the court with my death. As for the hinge of safety and peril today — what plan can be devised?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "If my error is so great, death alone can answer to the throne. This moment decides safety or ruin — what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 獻武王等曰：「未若還奉長樂，以安天下。」

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu and the others said: "Better to return and support Chang Le, to settle the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu and the others replied, "Better restore Chang Le to the throne and settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是還奉莊帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they restored Emperor Zhuang to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they restored Emperor Zhuang to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四日，輿駕入宮。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day, the imperial carriage entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day the emperor entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 于時或云榮欲遷都晉陽，或云欲肆兵大掠，迭相驚恐，人情駭震，京邑士子不一存，率皆逃竄，無敢出者。

translations.literal: At the time some said Rong wished to move the capital to Jinyang; others said he intended to let his troops plunder freely. Rumors bred terror upon terror. Hearts shook with alarm. Not one scholar of the capital remained in place — nearly all fled and hid, none daring to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors flew — Rong would move the capital to Jinyang, or let his troops loot at will. Panic fed on panic until the capital shook. Scholars fled en masse; scarcely a soul dared show his face in the streets.

sentences.zh: 直衞空虛，官守廢曠。

translations.literal: The direct guard was empty; official posts lay abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard stood empty; government offices were deserted.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，上書曰：「臣世荷蕃寄，征討累年，奉忠王室，志存效死。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant's clan for generations has borne the burden of frontier trust; for years I have marched on campaign, loyal to the royal house, resolved to give my life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Rong submitted a memorial: "My clan has served the dynasty for generations. I have campaigned year after year, loyal to the throne, ready to die in its service.

sentences.zh: 直以太后淫亂，孝明暴崩，遂率義兵，扶立社稷。

translations.literal: It was simply because the empress dowager's conduct was licentious and disordered and Emperor Xiaoming died suddenly that I led righteous troops to uphold the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the empress dowager's conduct brought disorder, and Emperor Xiaoming died suddenly, did I raise righteous troops to uphold the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 陛下登祚之始，人情未安，大兵交際，難可齊一，諸王朝貴橫死者眾，臣今粉軀不足塞往責以謝亡者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession, hearts were unsettled; great armies were in collision and could not be uniformly controlled. Many princes and nobles died violently. Your servant's crushed body now is insufficient to block past blame and answer to the dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first took the throne, hearts were unsettled and armies collided — discipline could not hold. Many princes and nobles died by violence. My own broken body cannot atone for what is past or answer to the dead.

sentences.zh: 然追榮褒德，謂之不朽，乞降天慈，微申私責。

translations.literal: Yet posthumous honors and the praise of virtue are called imperishable. I beg Heaven's kindness be lowered and my private plea be granted in small measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet posthumous honors endure; I beg Your Majesty's grace to hear this private plea.

sentences.zh: 無上王請追尊帝號，諸王、刺史乞贈三司，其位班三品請贈令僕，五品之官各贈方伯，六品已下及白民贈以鎮郡。

translations.literal: Prince Wushang — request posthumous elevation to emperor. Princes and regional inspectors — request promotion posthumously to the Three Excellencies. Those of third rank and above — request posthumous appointment as Director or Vice Director. Fifth-rank officials — each granted posthumously the title of regional lord. Sixth rank and below and commoners — grant posthumously titles of commandery and garrison chief.
translations.idiomatic: For Prince Wushang, posthumous imperial rank; for princes and prefects, the Three Excellencies; for third rank and above, directorships; for fifth rank, regional governorships; for sixth rank and below and commoners, commandery and garrison titles.

sentences.zh: 諸死者無後聽繼，即授封爵。

translations.literal: Those among the dead without heirs — permit adoption to continue their lines and immediately confer titles and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Where the dead left no heirs, permit adoption and confer titles at once.

sentences.zh: 均其高下節級別科，使恩洽存亡，有慰生死。」

translations.literal: Balance their high and low with graded categories so that grace reaches both living and dead and brings solace across the divide of life and death."
translations.idiomatic: Grade honors by rank so that grace reaches living and dead alike and brings comfort to both sides of the grave.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「覽表不勝鯁塞。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Having read the memorial, I cannot overcome the blockage in my throat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Reading your memorial fills my throat with grief.

sentences.zh: 朕德行無感，致茲酷濫，尋繹往事，貫切於懷。

translations.literal: My virtue and conduct moved no one, bringing about this cruel excess. Searching back through what has passed, it pierces my heart through and through.
translations.idiomatic: My own virtue has brought this bloodshed. Looking back on what has passed, the pain pierces me through.

sentences.zh: 可如所表。」

translations.literal: Let it be as set forth in the memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Let it be as you request."

sentences.zh: 自茲已後，贈終叨濫，庸人賤品，動至大官，為識者所不貴。

translations.literal: From this time forward, posthumous honors grew wanton and excessive; base men of low estate routinely received great offices — a thing those with discernment did not esteem.
translations.idiomatic: After this, posthumous honors became absurdly lavish; men of no merit routinely received high rank — something thoughtful observers scorned.

sentences.zh: 武定中，齊文襄王始革其失，追褒有典焉。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, Prince Wenxiang of Qi first reformed this abuse, and posthumous praise thereafter had proper standards.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era Prince Wenxiang of Qi first corrected the abuse and restored proper standards for posthumous honor.

sentences.zh: 榮啟帝遣使循城勞問，於是人情遂安，朝士逃亡者亦稍來歸闕。

translations.literal: Rong prompted the emperor to send envoys to make the rounds of the city with inquiries and comfort, whereupon hearts gradually settled. Court gentlemen who had fled also slowly returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Rong urged the emperor to send envoys through the city with words of comfort. Hearts steadied, and officials who had fled slowly drifted back to court.

sentences.zh: 榮又奏請番直，朔望之日引見三公、令僕、尚書、九卿及司州牧、河南尹、洛陽河陰執事之官，參論國治，經綸王道，以為常式。

translations.literal: Rong further memorialized requesting rotating watch duties: on the first and fifteenth of each month, to summon the Three Excellencies, Directors and Vice Directors, Masters of Writing, the Nine Ministers, the Governor of Sizhou, the Intendant of Henan, and the officials in charge at Luoyang and Heyin to consult on governing the state and ordering the royal way, making this a regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also petitioned for a rotating duty roster: on the first and fifteenth of each month the Three Excellencies, chief ministers, Masters of Writing, Nine Ministers, the Governor of Sizhou, the Intendant of Henan, and officials of Luoyang and Heyin would meet to debate governance — a standing custom thereafter.

sentences.zh: 五月，榮還晉陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Rong returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Rong returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔曰：「乾坤統物，星象贊其功；

translations.literal: In the seventh month, an edict said: "Heaven and Earth govern the myriad things; the stars and constellations proclaim their achievement;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict declared: "Heaven and Earth govern the myriad things, and the stars bear witness to their work;

sentences.zh: 皇王御運，股肱匡其業。

translations.literal: Emperors and kings steer the course of fate; arms and legs brace their enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: emperors and kings steer the course of fate, and loyal ministers brace their enterprise.

sentences.zh: 是以周道中缺，齊晉立濟世之忠；

translations.literal: Thus when the Zhou Way was in decline, Qi and Jin stood up with loyalty to rescue the age;
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou Way faltered, Qi and Jin rose with loyalty to rescue the age;

sentences.zh: 殷祚或虧，彭韋振救時之節。

translations.literal: when the Yin throne faltered, Peng and Wei raised the steadfastness of saving the times.
translations.idiomatic: when the Yin throne wavered, Peng and Wei answered with the steadfastness of men who save their age.

sentences.zh: 自前朝失御，厄運荐臻。

translations.literal: Since the previous court lost its grip, calamitous fortune has piled up one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Since the previous court lost its grip, calamity has piled upon calamity.

sentences.zh: 太原王榮爰戴朕躬，推臨萬國，勳踰伊霍，功格二儀，王室不壞，伊人是賴。

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan, Rong, has borne me up, pushed forward to oversee the myriad states — merit exceeding Yi and Huo, achievement reaching the two principles. The royal house stands unbroken; upon him the people rely.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Taiyuan Rong has borne me up and stepped forward to rule the myriad states — merit surpassing Yi Yin and Huo Guang, achievement reaching Heaven and Earth. The royal house still stands; the people lean on him.

sentences.zh: 可柱國大將軍、兼錄尚書事，餘如故。」

translations.literal: Appoint him Pillar of the State, Grand General, and Concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing; all else as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be appointed Pillar of the State, Grand General, and Concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing; all other offices remain as before."

sentences.zh: 時葛榮將向京師，眾號百萬。

translations.literal: At the time Ge Rong was marching on the capital, his forces claiming a million men.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ge Rong was marching on the capital at the head of an army said to number a million.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史李神軌閉門自守。

translations.literal: Li Shengui, Inspector of Xiang Province, shut his gates and held his ground.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengui, Inspector of Xiang Province, shut the city gates and held out alone.

sentences.zh: [5]賊鋒已過汲郡，所在村塢悉被殘略。

translations.literal: [5] The rebel vanguard had already passed Ji Commandery; every village stockade along the way was ravaged and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: [5] The rebel vanguard had already swept past Ji Commandery, ravaging every village stockade in its path.

sentences.zh: 榮啟求討之。

translations.literal: Rong memorialized requesting permission to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong petitioned for leave to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 九月，乃率精騎七千，馬皆有副，倍道兼行，東出滏口。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he then led seven thousand elite cavalry, each horse with a spare mount, traveling by forced marches day and night, eastward out through Fu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he led seven thousand elite horsemen, each with a spare mount, and raced east through Fu Pass by forced marches day and night.

sentences.zh: 葛榮為賊既久，橫行河北，時眾寡非敵，議者謂無制賊之理。

translations.literal: Ge Rong had been a bandit for a long time and rampaged across Hebei. At the time the numbers were unequal and not a match; commentators said there was no principle by which the bandits could be subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong had long led his rebels in rampaging across Hebei. Rong's force was vastly outnumbered, and observers said there was no way to bring such bandits to heel.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞之，喜見於色，乃令其眾曰：「此易與耳。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong heard of this, joy showed on his face, and he told his troops: "These will be easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong heard the news, delight showed on his face. He told his men, "These will be easy pickings.

sentences.zh: 諸人俱辦長繩，至便縛取。」

translations.literal: All of you prepare long ropes — when they arrive, bind and capture them."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone prepare long ropes — when they arrive, bind them up.

sentences.zh: 葛榮自鄴以北列陳數十里，箕張而進。

translations.literal: Ge Rong from Ye northward drew up his battle lines for several tens of li, advancing with wings spread like a winnowing basket.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong drew up his battle line north of Ye for miles on end and advanced with wings spread wide.

sentences.zh: 榮潛軍山谷為奇兵，分督將已上三人為一處，處有數百騎，令所在揚塵鼓譟，使賊不測多少。

translations.literal: Rong hid troops in the valleys as surprise forces. He divided supervising generals and above into groups of three at each point, each point with several hundred cavalry, ordering them everywhere to raise dust and beat drums in uproar so the bandits could not gauge how many there were.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hid troops in the valleys as a surprise force, grouping his senior commanders in threes with several hundred horsemen each, and ordered them to raise dust and beat drums everywhere so the rebels could not tell how many they faced.

sentences.zh: 又以人馬逼戰，刀不如棒，密勒軍士馬上各齎神棒一枚，[6]置於馬側。

translations.literal: He also considered that in close combat between men and horses, blades were inferior to clubs. He secretly ordered every soldier on horseback to carry one divine club, [6] kept at the horse's side.
translations.idiomatic: He also reasoned that in close combat between horse and man, a blade was no match for a club. In secret he ordered every cavalryman to carry a heavy iron club [6] at his saddle.

sentences.zh: 至於戰時，不聽斬級，以棒棒之而已，慮廢騰逐也。

translations.literal: When battle came, he forbade taking heads for tally — strike with the club, that alone — fearing that pursuit would be wasted.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he forbade taking heads for tally; strike with the club and nothing else, lest the chase be wasted.

sentences.zh: 乃分命壯勇所當衝突，號令嚴明，戰士同奮。

translations.literal: He then assigned the brave and strong to the points of assault. Orders were strict and clear; the warriors fought as one.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned his strongest men to the points of assault. Orders rang clear, and the warriors fought as one.

sentences.zh: 榮身自陷陳，出於賊後，表裏合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Rong himself plunged into the battle lines, emerging behind the bandits; inner and outer forces struck together and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rong himself plunged into the fray and emerged behind the rebel line; attacked from within and without, the enemy was shattered.

sentences.zh: 於陳擒葛榮，餘眾悉降。

translations.literal: On the field Ge Rong was captured; the remaining troops all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong was captured on the field; the rest surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 榮以賊徒既眾，若即分割，恐其疑懼，或更結聚，乃普告勒各從所樂，親屬相隨，任所居止。

translations.literal: Rong, considering that the bandit followers were numerous — if he divided them at once, he feared they would grow suspicious and afraid, or gather again — therefore issued a general proclamation allowing each to follow his own wish, kinsmen to stay together, and settle where they would.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host was vast; to divide them at once might breed fear and drive them to regroup. Rong therefore proclaimed that each man might go where he pleased, kinsmen keeping together, and settle where he chose.

sentences.zh: 於是羣情喜悅，登即四散，數十萬眾一朝散盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon all hearts rejoiced and at once scattered in every direction; several hundred thousand men dispersed in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts lifted; in a single morning several hundred thousand men scattered to the winds.

sentences.zh: 待出百里之外，乃始分道押領，隨便安置，咸得其宜。

translations.literal: After they had gone beyond a hundred li, he then began to divide them into routes under escort and settle them as convenient — all found fitting placement.
translations.idiomatic: Only after they had spread a hundred li did he begin escorting them by separate routes and settling each where it suited — all to good effect.

sentences.zh: 擢其渠帥，量力授用，新附者咸安。

translations.literal: He promoted their chieftains and assigned duties according to capacity; the newly attached all found peace.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted rebel chieftains and assigned posts according to their ability; the newly surrendered settled into peace.

sentences.zh: 時人服其處分機速。

translations.literal: People of the time admired the speed and decisiveness of his disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries marveled at the speed and soundness of his handling.

sentences.zh: 乃檻車送葛榮赴闕。

translations.literal: He then sent Ge Rong to court in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong was sent to the capital in a caged cart.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「功格天地，錫命之位必崇；

translations.literal: An edict said: "When achievement reaches Heaven and Earth, the rank bestowed by grace must be exalted;
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "When merit reaches Heaven and Earth, the rank conferred must be exalted;

sentences.zh: 道濟生民，褒賞之名宜大。

translations.literal: when the Way succors the living people, the name of praise and reward should be great.
translations.idiomatic: when the Way succors the people, the name of reward must be great.

sentences.zh: 是以有莘贊亳，不次之號爰歸；

translations.literal: Thus when Youxin assisted Bo, the extraordinary title was his to receive;
translations.idiomatic: When Youxin assisted Tang at Bo, an extraordinary title was his due;

sentences.zh: 渭叟翼周，殊世之班載集。

translations.literal: when the old man of the Wei assisted Zhou, ranks beyond the age were heaped upon him.
translations.idiomatic: when the old man of the Wei River aided Zhou, ranks beyond any age were heaped upon him.

sentences.zh: 況導源積石，襲構崐山，門踵英猷，弼成鴻業，抗高天之摧柱，振厚地之絕維，德冠五侯，勳高九伯者哉！

translations.literal: How much more one who guides the source from Jishi, inherits the structure of Kunlun, in succession follows heroic designs, assists in completing the great enterprise, upholds the collapsing pillar of the high heavens, and braces the severed cords of the thick earth — virtue crowning the five marquises, merit towering above the nine lords!
translations.idiomatic: How much more one who draws his source from Jishi, inherits Kunshan's foundation, follows in the footsteps of heroic forebears, and helps complete a great enterprise — who props up Heaven's falling pillar and braces Earth's snapped cords, whose virtue crowns the five marquises and whose merit towers over the nine lords!

sentences.zh: 太原王榮代荷蕃寵，世載忠烈，入匡頹運，出剿元兇，使積年之霧倏焉滌蕩，數載之塵一朝清謐。

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan, Rong, for generations has borne the frontier favor; his clan for ages has carried loyalty and fierce devotion. Within he has righted a failing fortune; without he has exterminated the chief villain — making years of accumulated mist suddenly washed clean, years of dust in a single morning restored to clarity and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Taiyuan Rong, favored by the throne for generations, his house long known for loyalty and valor — within he has righted a failing age, without he has destroyed the arch-rebel — years of murk washed away in an instant, years of dust stilled in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 燕恒既泰，趙魏還蘇，比績況功，古今莫二，若不式稽舊典，增是禮數，將何以昭德報功，遠明國範？

translations.literal: Yan and Heng are already at peace; Zhao and Wei have revived — comparing achievements and weighing merit, none in past or present is his second. If we do not follow the old statutes and increase these honors, how shall we display virtue and repay merit, and make the nation's model clear afar?
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Heng stand at peace; Zhao and Wei breathe again — matched against the records of past and present, his like is second to none. If we do not follow ancient precedent and enlarge these honors, how shall we proclaim his virtue, repay his merit, and hold him up as the nation's model?

sentences.zh: 可大丞相、都督河北畿外諸軍事，增邑一萬戶，通前三萬，餘官悉如故。」

translations.literal: Appoint him Grand Chancellor and Commander of All Military Affairs in Hebei and Beyond the Capital Region; increase his fief by ten thousand households, thirty thousand in total with the previous grants; all other offices remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Grand Chancellor and Commander of All Military Affairs in Hebei and beyond the capital region; increase his fief by ten thousand households, thirty thousand in all; all other offices remain as before."

sentences.zh: 初，榮之將討葛榮也，軍次襄垣，遂令軍士列圍大獵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Rong was about to campaign against Ge Rong, the army halted at Xiangyuan, and he ordered the soldiers to form an encircling hunt on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: Before the campaign against Ge Rong, the army halted at Xiangyuan, and Rong ordered a great encircling hunt.

sentences.zh: 有雙兔起於馬前，榮乃躍馬彎弓而誓之曰：「中之則擒葛榮，不中則否。」

translations.literal: A pair of hares rose before his horse. Rong leapt into the saddle, bent his bow, and swore: "If I hit them, Ge Rong will be captured; if I miss, he will not."
translations.idiomatic: Two hares burst up before his horse. Rong spurred forward, strung his bow, and swore: "If I hit them, Ge Rong will be taken; if I miss, he will not.

sentences.zh: 既而並應弦而殪，三軍咸悅。

translations.literal: Immediately both fell to the released strings. The whole army rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Both fell to a single volley. The whole army exulted.

sentences.zh: 及破賊之後，即命立碑於其所，號「雙兔碑」。

translations.literal: After defeating the bandits, he immediately ordered a stele erected on the spot, called the "Stele of the Twin Hares."
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he ordered a stele raised on the spot, called the Stele of the Twin Hares.

sentences.zh: 榮將戰之夜，夢一人從葛榮索千牛刀，而葛榮初不肯與。

translations.literal: On the night before the battle, Rong dreamed that a man demanded a thousand-ox blade from Ge Rong, but at first Ge Rong refused to give it.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of battle Rong dreamed that a man demanded Ge Rong's thousand-ox blade, and at first Ge Rong refused.

sentences.zh: 此人自稱我是道武皇帝，汝何敢違。

translations.literal: The man declared: "I am Emperor Daowu — how dare you disobey?"
translations.idiomatic: The man declared, "I am Emperor Daowu — how dare you refuse?"

sentences.zh: 葛榮乃奉刀，此人手持授榮。

translations.literal: Ge Rong then presented the blade; the man took it in hand and gave it to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong surrendered the blade; the man took it and placed it in Rong's hand.

sentences.zh: 既寤而喜，自知必勝。

translations.literal: When he awoke he rejoiced, knowing in himself that victory was certain.
translations.idiomatic: He woke rejoicing, certain of victory.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「我皇魏道契神元，德光靈範，源先二象，化穆五才，玉歷與日月惟休，金鼎共乾坤俱永。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Our Great Wei — its Way accords with the divine origin, its virtue shines with the numinous model, its source precedes the two images, its transformation harmonizes the five talents. The jade calendar shares repose with sun and moon; the golden cauldron endures with Heaven and Earth alike.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "Our Great Wei — its Way joins with the divine origin, its virtue shines with the numinous model, its source predates the two primal forces, its transforming power harmonizes the five talents. Its jade calendar shares eternity with sun and moon; its golden cauldron endures with Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 而正光之末，皇運時屯，百揆咸亂，九宮失敍，朝野撫膺，士女嗟怨，遂使四海土崩，九區瓦解。

translations.literal: Yet at the end of the Zhenguang era the imperial fortune met hardship in its season; the hundred offices all fell into disorder, the nine palaces lost their sequence. Court and countryside beat their breasts; gentlemen and women sighed in grievance — until the four seas crumbled like earth and the nine regions dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the end of the Zhenguang era imperial fortune faltered; the hundred offices fell into chaos, the nine palaces lost their order. Court and countryside beat their breasts in anguish until the four seas crumbled and the nine regions split apart.

sentences.zh: 逆賊杜周，虔劉燕代；

translations.literal: The rebel Du Zhou slaughtered with fervor in Yan and Dai;
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Du Zhou ravaged Yan and Dai;

sentences.zh: 妖寇葛榮，假噬魏趙。

translations.literal: the demonic bandit Ge Rong borrowed his bite to devour Wei and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: the demonic bandit Ge Rong preyed upon Wei and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 常山、易水，戎鼓夜驚；

translations.literal: At Changshan and Yishui, war drums alarmed the night;
translations.idiomatic: At Changshan and Yishui war drums shattered the night;

sentences.zh: 冰井、叢臺，胡塵晝合。

translations.literal: at Bingjing and Congtai, barbarian dust blotted out the day.
translations.idiomatic: at Bingjing and Congtai barbarian dust blotted out the day.

sentences.zh: 朔南久已丘墟，河北殆成灰燼。

translations.literal: The north and south had long lain in ruins; Hebei was nearly reduced to ash and ember.
translations.idiomatic: North and south had long stood in ruins; Hebei was nearly ash.

sentences.zh: 宗廟懷匪安之慮，社稷急不測之憂。

translations.literal: The ancestral temples harbored thoughts of no peace; the altars of state faced urgent, unforeseeable dread.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temples knew no peace; the altars of state faced dread beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 大丞相、太原王榮道鏡域中，德光區外，神昭藏往，思實知來，義踵先勳，忠資曩烈。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor, Prince of Taiyuan, Rong — his Way mirrors the realm within, his virtue shines beyond the borders; his spirit illuminates what is hidden in the past, his thought truly knows what is to come. In righteousness he follows the former achievements; in loyalty he draws on the fierce devotion of old.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Chancellor, Prince of Taiyuan Rong — his Way mirrors the realm, his virtue shines beyond its borders; his spirit reads the hidden past, his mind discerns what is to come. In righteousness he follows the achievements of old; in loyalty he draws on the valor of his forebears.

sentences.zh: 遂能大建義謀，收集忠勇，熊羆競逐，虎豹爭先，軒翥南溟，摶風北極，氣震林原，勢動山岳，弔民伐罪，殲此鯨鯢。

translations.literal: Thus he could greatly raise righteous designs, gather the loyal and brave — bears and badgers raced in pursuit, tigers and leopards vied to lead — soaring like wings over the southern sea, beating the wind at the northern pole; his spirit shook forests and plains, his momentum moved mountains and peaks; comforting the people and punishing crime, he exterminated these whale-monsters.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a righteous design, gathered the loyal and brave — bears and badgers raced in pursuit, tigers and leopards vied for the van — soaring over the southern sea, beating the wind at the northern pole; his spirit shook forest and field, his force moved mountains; comforting the people and punishing the guilty, he destroyed these monsters of the deep.

sentences.zh: 戮卒多於長平，積器高於熊耳。

translations.literal: Slain soldiers outnumbered those at Changping; piled weapons rose higher than Mount Xiong'er.
translations.idiomatic: The slain outnumbered those at Changping; piled weapons rose higher than Mount Xiong'er.

sentences.zh: 秦晉聞聲而喪膽，齊莒側聽而讋息。

translations.literal: Qin and Jin heard the report and lost their gall; Qi and Ju listened from the side and held their breath in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Jin heard the news and lost heart; Qi and Ju listened in dread and held their breath.

sentences.zh: 中興之業是乎再隆，太平之基茲焉更始。

translations.literal: The enterprise of restoration thereby rose again; the foundation of great peace here began anew.
translations.idiomatic: The work of restoration rose again; the foundation of peace began anew.

sentences.zh: 雖復伊霍宣翼之功，桓文崇贊之道，何足以髣髴鴻蹤，比勳盛烈。

translations.literal: Even the assisting merit of Yi and Huo, the exalted supporting Way of Huan and Wen — how could they suffice to glimpse the great tracks, or compare with such towering achievement and blazing glory?
translations.idiomatic: Even the assisting merit of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, the exalted patronage of Duke Huan and Duke Wen — how could they glimpse such footprints, or compare with merit so blazing and great?

sentences.zh: 道格普天，仁沾率土，振古以來，未有其比。

translations.literal: His Way reaches the universal heavens; his benevolence moistens all within the land. Since the shaking of antiquity, none has been his equal.
translations.idiomatic: His Way reaches all under Heaven; his benevolence touches every corner of the realm. Since time out of mind, none has been his equal.

sentences.zh: 若不廣錫山河，大開土宇，何以表大義之崇高，標盛德之廣遠？

translations.literal: If we do not broadly bestow mountains and rivers and greatly expand his domain, how shall we display the loftiness of great righteousness and mark the breadth and reach of supreme virtue?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not grant him broad dominion over mountains and rivers and enlarge his realm, how shall we proclaim the loftiness of his righteousness and mark the far-reaching scope of his supreme virtue?

sentences.zh: 可以冀州之長樂、相州之南趙、定州之博陵、滄州之浮陽、平州之遼西、燕州之上谷、幽州之漁陽等七郡，各萬戶通前滿十萬戶為太原國邑。」

translations.literal: Let Chang Le in Ji Province, Nan Zhao in Xiang Province, Boling in Ding Province, Fuyang in Cang Province, Liaoxi in Ping Province, Shanggu in Yan Province, and Yuyang in You Province — these seven commanderies, ten thousand households each, together with the previous grants making one hundred thousand households in all, serve as the fief of the State of Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The seven commanderies of Chang Le in Ji Province, Nan Zhao in Xiang Province, Boling in Ding Province, Fuyang in Cang Province, Liaoxi in Ping Province, Shanggu in Yan Province, and Yuyang in You Province — ten thousand households each, one hundred thousand in all with previous grants — were to form the fief of the State of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 又進位太師，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Grand Preceptor; all else remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Preceptor; all other offices remained as before."

sentences.zh: 建義初，北海王元顥南奔蕭衍，衍乃立為魏主，資以兵將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao fled south to Xiao Yan, who then installed him as ruler of Wei and supplied him with troops and generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao fled south to Xiao Yan, who set him up as ruler of Wei and furnished him with troops and commanders.

sentences.zh: 時邢杲寇亂三齊，與顥應接。

translations.literal: At the time Xing Gao was raiding and ravaging the Three Qi, coordinating with Hao in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xing Gao was ravaging the Three Qi, acting in concert with Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以顥孤弱，不以為慮。

translations.literal: The court regarded Hao as isolated and weak and did not take him as a concern.
translations.idiomatic: The court considered Yuan Hao isolated and weak and gave him little thought.

sentences.zh: 永安二年春，[7]詔大將軍元穆先平齊地，然後回師征顥。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Yong'an, [7] an edict ordered Grand General Yuan Mu first to pacify the Qi region, then to turn his army and campaign against Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Yong'an, [7] an edict ordered Grand General Yuan Mu to pacify Qi first, then turn his army against Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥以大軍未還，乘虛徑進，既陷梁國，鼓行而西，滎陽、虎牢並皆不守。

translations.literal: Hao, because the great army had not yet returned, seized the opening and pressed straight forward. Having taken Liang State, he marched west with drums beating; Xingyang and Hulao both fell without defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao, seeing the main army still abroad, drove straight through the gap. He took Liang State and marched west with drums beating; Xingyang and Hulao both fell without a fight.

sentences.zh: 五月，車駕出幸河北。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the imperial carriage went out to visit Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor withdrew north into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 事出不虞，天下改望。

translations.literal: The affair arose beyond expectation; the realm shifted its hopes.
