translations.idiomatic: The crisis came without warning, and the realm turned its hopes elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 榮聞之，即時馳傳朝行宮於上黨之長子，行其部分。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this he immediately raced by post relay toward the traveling palace at Changzi in Shangdang, deploying his divisions as he went.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong heard the news he raced by post toward the traveling palace at Changzi in Shangdang, deploying his divisions as he went.

sentences.zh: 輿駕於是南轅，榮為前驅，旬日之間，兵馬大集，資糧器仗，繼踵而至。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage thereupon turned south; Rong served as vanguard. Within ten days troops and horses massed in great numbers, and provisions, grain, weapons, and gear arrived in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned south; Rong rode at the van. Within ten days troops and horses massed, and provisions, grain, weapons, and gear poured in without pause.

sentences.zh: 天穆既平邢杲，亦渡河以會車駕。

translations.literal: Tianmu, having already pacified Xing Gao, likewise crossed the river to join the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu, having pacified Xing Gao, crossed the river to join the emperor.

sentences.zh: 顥都督宗正珍孫、河內太守元襲固守不降，榮攻而克之，斬珍孫、元襲以徇。

translations.literal: Hao's commander Zongzheng Zhensun and Intendant of Henei Yuan Xi held firm and refused to surrender. Rong attacked and took them, beheading Zhensun and Yuan Xi as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao's commanders Zongzheng Zhensun and Intendant of Henei Yuan Xi held out and refused to yield. Rong stormed the place, beheaded both men, and displayed their heads as a warning.

sentences.zh: 帝幸河內城。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Henei city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took refuge in Henei city.

sentences.zh: 榮與顥相持於河上，顥令都督安豐王延明緣河據守。

translations.literal: Rong and Hao faced each other across the river. Hao ordered his commander Prince of Anfeng Yanming to hold the line along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Yuan Hao faced each other across the river. Yuan Hao ordered Prince of Anfeng Yanming to hold the river line.

sentences.zh: 榮既未有舟船，不得即渡，議欲還北，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Rong, having no boats yet, could not cross at once. Counsel favored returning north and planning a later effort.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had no boats and could not cross at once. Some counseled returning north to plan another attempt.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎楊侃、高道穆等並謂大軍若還，失天下之望，固執以為不可。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others all said that if the great army returned, it would lose the realm's hopes, and they stubbornly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate Yang Kan, Gao Daomu, and others argued that a retreat would forfeit the realm's trust and firmly insisted it must not happen.

sentences.zh: 語在侃等傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in the biographies of Kan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biographies of Kan and the others.

sentences.zh: 屬馬渚諸楊云有小船數艘，求為鄉導，榮乃令都督尒朱兆等率精騎夜濟，登岸奮擊。

translations.literal: Just then the Yang clan of Mazhu said they had several small boats and asked to serve as guides. Rong then ordered his commander Er Zhuba and others to lead elite cavalry across by night, land on shore, and strike with fury.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Yang clan of Mazhu offered several small boats and asked to guide the crossing. Rong ordered Er Zhuba and others to lead elite cavalry across by night, land on the far shore, and strike hard.

sentences.zh: 顥子領軍將軍冠受率馬步五千拒戰，兆大破之，臨陳擒冠受。

translations.literal: Hao's son, General of the Central Army Guanshou, led five thousand horse and foot to resist. Zhuba routed them utterly and captured Guanshou on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao's son Guanshou, General of the Central Army, led five thousand horse and foot to resist. Zhuba shattered them and took Guanshou on the field.

sentences.zh: 延明聞冠受見擒，遂自逃散，顥便率麾下南奔。

translations.literal: When Yanming heard that Guanshou had been captured, he fled and scattered on his own. Hao then led his followers in flight south.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanming learned Guanshou had been taken, his force broke and fled. Yuan Hao led his followers south in retreat.

sentences.zh: 事在其傳。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in his biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 車駕渡河，入居華林園。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage crossed the river and entered residence at Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed the river and took up residence in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「周武奉時，藉十亂以纂曆；

translations.literal: An edict said: "King Wu of Zhou received the mandate of the times and, relying on the ten disordered ones, seized the calendar of rule;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "King Wu of Zhou received Heaven's mandate and, with the aid of ten disordered lords, seized the throne;

sentences.zh: 漢祖先天，資三傑以除暴。

translations.literal: the Ancestor of Han preceded Heaven and, relying on the Three Heroes, removed tyranny.
translations.idiomatic: the Founder of Han moved before Heaven and, with the Three Heroes at his side, overthrew tyranny.

sentences.zh: 理民濟治，斯道未爽。

translations.literal: To order the people and succor governance — this Way has not failed.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the people and set the realm in order — this principle has never failed.

sentences.zh: 使持節、柱國大將軍、大丞相、太原王榮，蘊伏風煙，抱含日月，總奇正以成術，兼文武而為資。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Pillar of the State, Grand General, Grand Chancellor, Prince of Taiyuan, Rong — he harbored within himself wind and mist, embraced sun and moon, gathered the orthodox and the unorthodox to complete his art, and joined civil and martial as his resources.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Pillar of the State, Grand General, Grand Chancellor, Prince of Taiyuan Rong — he concealed his power like wind and mist, held sun and moon within him, united orthodox and unorthodox stratagems into one art, and drew on both civil and martial gifts as his strength.

sentences.zh: 昔處亂朝，韜光戢翼，秣馬冀北，厲兵晉陽，佇龍顏而振腕，想日角以歎息。

translations.literal: Formerly in a disordered court he hid his light and folded his wings, fed his horses north of Ji, sharpened his weapons at Jinyang, waited for the dragon countenance and flexed his wrist, thought of the sun-horn brow and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in a court gone to ruin, he hid his light and bided his time — fed his horses north of Ji, sharpened his weapons at Jinyang, waited for the emperor's face and clenched his fist, dreamed of a sovereign marked by Heaven and sighed.

sentences.zh: 忠勇奮發，虎士如林，義功始立，所向風靡。

translations.literal: Loyal and brave, he roused himself to action; tiger warriors stood thick as a forest. Righteous achievement was first established; wherever he turned, the wind blew all before him.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and brave, he roused himself to action; his tiger warriors stood thick as a forest. Righteous achievement was his from the first; wherever he turned, resistance crumbled like chaff.

sentences.zh: 故能芟夷羣惡，振此頹綱，俾朕寡昧，獲承鴻緒。

translations.literal: Thus he could mow down the multitude of evils, raise up this failing cord of order, and enable me, dull and dim, to inherit the great thread of succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he cut down the hosts of evil, raised this failing order from ruin, and let me — dull and unworthy — inherit the great succession.

sentences.zh: 雖大位克正，而眾盜未息。

translations.literal: Although the great throne was rightly secured, the many bandits had not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Though the throne was rightly secured, bandits still roamed the land.

sentences.zh: 葛榮跋扈，仍亂中原，建旗伐罪，授首殲馘。

translations.literal: Ge Rong was overbearing and lawless, still troubling the Central Plain. Rong raised his banner to punish crime, took his head, and annihilated his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong ran rampant and still ravaged the Central Plain. Rong raised the banner of punishment, took his head, and destroyed his army.

sentences.zh: 元顥凶頑，構成巨釁，阻弄吳楚，虧汙宗社。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao was fierce and stubborn, contriving a great offense, obstructing and toying with Wu and Chu, defiling and staining the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao was vicious and obstinate, contriving a great rebellion, stirring trouble in Wu and Chu and staining the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 朕徙御北徂，劬勞鞍甲。

translations.literal: I moved the imperial carriage northward, toiling in saddle and armor.
translations.idiomatic: I withdrew north myself, weary in saddle and armor.

sentences.zh: 王聞難星奔，一舉大定，下洽民和，上匡王室。

translations.literal: The prince, hearing of the crisis, raced like a star; in one stroke he settled all greatly. Below, the people were harmonized; above, the royal house was righted.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, hearing of the crisis, raced to the rescue and settled all in one stroke — below, the people found peace; above, the throne was saved.

sentences.zh: 鴻勳巨績，書契所未紀；

translations.literal: Great merit and towering achievement — what writing and tallies have never recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Merit so great and achievement so towering that no record in writing or tally has ever matched it;

sentences.zh: 飲至策勳，事絕於比況。

translations.literal: feasting at the victory rite and enfeoffing by merit — the affair stands beyond comparison.
translations.idiomatic: victory feasts and merit rolls alike find no parallel in history.

sentences.zh: 非常之功，必有非常之賞，可天柱大將軍。

translations.literal: Extraordinary achievement must receive extraordinary reward. Appoint him Heaven-Pillar Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary achievement demands extraordinary reward. Let him be appointed Heaven-Pillar Grand General.

sentences.zh: 此官雖訪古無聞，今員未有，太祖已前增置此號，式遵典故，用錫殊禮。

translations.literal: Although inquiry into antiquity finds no mention of this office and no incumbent exists today, before Emperor Taizu this title was newly established. Following ancient precedent, let it be used to bestow a special honor.
translations.idiomatic: Though antiquity knows no such office and none holds it today, the title was established before Emperor Taizu. Following ancient precedent, let it serve as a special honor.

sentences.zh: 又宜開土宇，可增封十萬，通前二十萬，加前後部羽葆鼓吹。

translations.literal: It is also fitting to expand his domain. Increase his fief by one hundred thousand households, two hundred thousand in all with previous grants, and add front and rear guard feather-canopy processional music.
translations.idiomatic: His domain should also be enlarged: increase his fief by one hundred thousand households, two hundred thousand in all, and grant front and rear guard feather-canopy processional music.

sentences.zh: 餘如故。」

translations.literal: All else remains as before."
translations.idiomatic: All other offices remain as before.

sentences.zh: 榮尋還晉陽。

translations.literal: Rong soon returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong soon returned to Jinyang."

sentences.zh: 先是，葛榮枝黨韓婁仍據幽平二州，榮遣都督侯淵討斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ge Rong's branch follower Han Lou still held the two provinces of You and Ping. Rong sent his commander Hou Yuan to campaign against and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ge Rong's lieutenant Han Lou still held You and Ping provinces. Rong sent Hou Yuan against him and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥万俟醜奴、蕭寶夤擁眾豳涇，兇勢日盛。

translations.literal: At the time the bandit chiefs Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin gathered crowds at Bin and Jing; their fierce momentum grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the rebel chiefs Moqi Chounu and Xiao Baoyin held Bin and Jing with large forces, and their power grew daily.

sentences.zh: 榮遣其從子天光為雍州刺史，令率都督賀拔岳、侯莫陳悅等總眾入關討之。

translations.literal: Rong sent his nephew Tianguang as Inspector of Yong Province and ordered him to lead the commanders Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and others with combined forces into the passes to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent his nephew Tianguang as Inspector of Yong Province and ordered him to lead Heba Yue, Houmochen Yue, and other commanders through the passes against them.

sentences.zh: 天光既至雍州，以眾少不敵，逡巡未集。

translations.literal: When Tianguang reached Yong Province, because his numbers were few and no match for the enemy, he hesitated and did not gather his forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang reached Yong Province he found his force too small to match the enemy and hesitated without gathering his troops.

sentences.zh: 榮大怒，遣其騎兵參軍劉貴馳驛詣軍，加天光杖罰。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly enraged and sent his cavalry adjutant Liu Gui racing by post relay to the army to impose beating punishment on Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was furious and sent his cavalry adjutant Liu Gui racing by post to the army to have Tianguang beaten.

sentences.zh: 天光等大懼，乃進討，連破之，擒醜奴、寶夤，並檻車送闕。

translations.literal: Tianguang and the others were greatly afraid and therefore advanced to campaign, defeating them in succession, capturing Chounu and Baoyin, and sending both to court in caged carts.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang and his men were terrified and advanced to fight. They won victory after victory, captured Chounu and Baoyin, and sent both to the capital in caged carts.

sentences.zh: 天光又擒王慶雲、万俟道樂，關西悉平。

translations.literal: Tianguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daole, and all west of the passes was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang also captured Wang Qingyun and Moqi Daole, and all west of the passes was pacified.

sentences.zh: 於是天下大難，便以盡矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great calamities of the realm were considered to have ended.
translations.idiomatic: It seemed the great calamities of the realm had at last come to an end.

sentences.zh: 榮性好獵，不舍寒暑，至於列圍而進，必須齊一，雖遇阻險，不得回避，虎豹逸圍者坐死。

translations.literal: Rong by nature loved the hunt and never ceased whether in cold or heat. When advancing in drawn encirclement, the line had to be uniform. Even if obstacles were met, none might evade. Whoever let a tiger or leopard escape the ring was punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Rong loved the hunt and never stopped, winter or summer. When the beaters closed the ring every man had to hold the line — no evasion, even over rough ground. Anyone who let a tiger or leopard break out was put to death.

sentences.zh: 其下甚苦之。

translations.literal: Those under his command suffered greatly from this.
translations.idiomatic: His men suffered greatly under this.

sentences.zh: 太宰元天穆從容謂榮曰：「大王勳濟天下，四方無事，惟宜調政養民，順時蒐狩，何必盛夏馳逐，傷犯和氣。」

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu said calmly to Rong: "Great King, your merit has succored the realm; the four quarters are without trouble. You should only adjust governance and nourish the people, and hunt according to the season. Why must you race in pursuit in the height of summer and harm and violate the harmonious qi?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuan Tianmu said gently to Rong, "Your merit has saved the realm; the four quarters are at peace. You should govern wisely, nourish the people, and hunt in season. Why race through the midsummer heat and upset the balance of the year?"

sentences.zh: 榮便攘肘謂天穆曰：「太后女主，不能自正，推奉天子者，此是人臣常節。

translations.literal: Rong then jostled Tianmu with his elbow and said: "The empress dowager is a woman ruler who could not set herself right. To raise up and support the Son of Heaven — this is the constant duty of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Rong jostled Tianmu with his elbow and said, "The empress dowager was a woman who could not govern herself. Raising up the Son of Heaven is what any loyal subject does.

sentences.zh: 葛榮之徒，本是奴才，乘時作亂，妄自署假，譬如奴走，擒獲便休。

translations.literal: Men like Ge Rong were originally slaves who seized the moment to rebel and presumptuously appointed themselves to false titles — like a runaway slave: once captured, the matter ends.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Ge Rong were slaves who seized their moment, made up titles for themselves, and rebelled — like a runaway bondman: catch him and the trouble is over.

sentences.zh: 頃來受國大寵，未能開拓境土，混一海內，何宜今日便言勳也！

translations.literal: Recently I have received the state's great favor, yet I have not opened and expanded the borders or unified all within the seas. How is it fitting to speak of merit today!
translations.idiomatic: I have received the state's greatest favor, yet I have not expanded the borders or unified the realm. How can anyone speak of merit now!

sentences.zh: 如聞朝士猶自寬縱，今秋欲共兄戒勒士馬，校獵嵩原，令貪污朝貴入圍搏虎。

translations.literal: I hear that court gentlemen are still indulging themselves. This autumn I wish to join you, brother, in drilling troops and horses and holding a great hunt on the Song plain, making the greedy and corrupt court nobles enter the ring to wrestle tigers.
translations.idiomatic: I hear court officials still indulge themselves. This autumn I mean to drill troops with you on the Song plain and drive the corrupt nobles into the ring to wrestle tigers.

sentences.zh: 仍出魯陽，歷三荊，悉擁生蠻北填六鎮。

translations.literal: Then I will go out from Luyang, pass through the Three Jing regions, and drive all the living barbarians north to fill the Six Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Then I will march from Luyang through the Three Jing regions and drive the barbarians north to repopulate the Six Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 回軍之際，因平汾胡。

translations.literal: On the return march I will take the occasion to pacify the Fen Hu.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march I will pacify the Fen Hu as well.

sentences.zh: 明年簡練精騎，分出江淮，蕭衍若降，乞萬戶侯。

translations.literal: Next year I will select and drill elite cavalry and send columns south of the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan submits, I ask only for a marquisate of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Next year I will drill elite cavalry and send columns south of the Yangtze and Huai. If Xiao Yan submits, a marquisate of ten thousand households is all I ask.

sentences.zh: 如其不降，徑渡數千騎，便往縛取。

translations.literal: If he does not submit, I will cross directly with several thousand cavalry and go bind and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: If he refuses, I will cross with a few thousand horsemen and bind him where he stands.

sentences.zh: 待六合寧一，八表無塵，然後共兄奉天子，巡四方，觀風俗，布政教，如此乃可稱勳耳。

translations.literal: Wait until the six directions are settled as one and the eight borderlands are without dust; then together with you, brother, we will support the Son of Heaven, tour the four quarters, observe customs, and spread governance and teaching — only then may one speak of merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the six directions are one and the eight borderlands are at peace, then you and I will support the Son of Heaven, tour the realm, observe its customs, and spread governance and teaching — only then will there be merit worth the name.

sentences.zh: 今若止獵，兵士懈怠，安可復用也。」

translations.literal: If we stop hunting now, the soldiers will grow slack — how can they be used again?"
translations.idiomatic: Stop the hunt now and the soldiers grow slack — how then can they be used again?"

sentences.zh: 榮身雖居外，恒遙制朝廷，廣布親戚，列為左右，伺察動靜，小大必知。

translations.literal: Although Rong's person dwelt outside the capital, he constantly controlled the court from afar. He spread his kinsmen widely and set them at left and right, watching and observing every movement — matters great and small he always knew.
translations.idiomatic: Though Rong lived outside the capital he controlled the court from afar. He planted kinsmen on every side to watch all that moved — nothing great or small escaped him.

sentences.zh: 或有僥倖求官者，皆詣榮承候，得其啟請，無不遂之。

translations.literal: If any sought office by luck and favor, all went to Rong to attend upon him. Once they obtained his memorial and request, nothing failed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone seeking office by favor went first to Rong. With his endorsement, no request failed.

sentences.zh: 曾關補定州曲陽縣令，吏部尚書李神儁以階懸不奉，別更擬人。

translations.literal: Once he intervened to appoint the magistrate of Quyang County in Ding Province. Director of the Masters of Writing Li Shenjun, because the rank was too high, did not comply and instead proposed another man.
translations.idiomatic: Once he intervened to appoint the magistrate of Quyang in Ding Province. Director of the Masters of Writing Li Shenjun, finding the rank inappropriate, refused and proposed another candidate.

sentences.zh: 榮聞大怒，即遣其所補者往奪其任。

translations.literal: When Rong heard of this he was greatly enraged and immediately sent the man he had appointed to go seize the post.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was furious and sent his appointee to seize the post by force.

sentences.zh: 榮使入京，雖復微蔑，朝貴見之莫不傾靡；

translations.literal: When Rong's envoys entered the capital, though they were again slight and contemptuous, no court noble who saw them failed to bow and yield;
translations.idiomatic: When Rong's agents entered the capital, however slight their manner, no court noble failed to bow before them;

sentences.zh: 及至闕下，未得通奏，恃榮威勢，至乃忿怒。

translations.literal: yet when they reached the palace gates and could not obtain audience to report, relying on Rong's prestige and power, they even grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: yet at the palace gates, denied audience, they raged on Rong's authority alone.

sentences.zh: 榮曾啟北人為河南諸州，莊帝未許，天穆入見，面啟曰：「天柱既有大功，若請普代天下官屬，恐陛下亦不得違之，如何啟數人為州，便停不用！」

translations.literal: Rong once memorialized requesting northerners for the various provinces of Henan. Emperor Zhuang did not approve. Tianmu entered audience and reported to his face, saying: "The Heaven-Pillar has such great achievement — if he requested to replace all officials throughout the realm, I fear Your Majesty could not refuse either. How is it that he requests a few men for provincial posts and you stop and do not use them!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong once petitioned to install northerners in the Henan provinces. Emperor Zhuang refused. Tianmu entered audience and said to his face, "The Heaven-Pillar has done so much — if he asked to replace every official in the realm, could Your Majesty refuse? Yet he asks for a few provincial posts and you turn him down!

sentences.zh: 帝正色曰：「天柱若不為人臣，朕亦須代；

translations.literal: The emperor said sternly: "If the Heaven-Pillar is no longer a subject, then I too must be replaced;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said coldly, "If the Heaven-Pillar is no longer my subject, then replace me too;

sentences.zh: 如其猶存臣節，無代天下百官理。

translations.literal: if he still preserves the integrity of a subject, there is no principle by which he may replace all officials throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: if he still holds to the duty of a subject, he has no business replacing every official in the realm.

sentences.zh: 此事復何足論。」

translations.literal: This matter is again not worth discussing."
translations.idiomatic: That is not worth another word.

sentences.zh: 榮聞所啟不允，大為恚恨，曰：「天子由誰得立？

translations.literal: When Rong heard that his memorial was not granted, he was greatly resentful and said: "By whom was the Son of Heaven established?
translations.idiomatic: When Rong learned his petition was denied he was furious. "By whose hand was the emperor raised to the throne?

sentences.zh: 今乃不用我語。」

translations.literal: Now he will not use my words."
translations.idiomatic: And now he will not heed me.

sentences.zh: 莊帝外迫於榮，恒怏怏不悅，兼懲榮河陰之事，恐終難保。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang, outwardly pressed by Rong, was constantly displeased and unhappy. He also took warning from Rong's affair at Heyin and feared he could not be preserved in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly pressed by Rong, Emperor Zhuang brooded in constant displeasure. He remembered Heyin as well and feared he could not survive in the end.

sentences.zh: 又城陽王徽、侍中李彧等欲擅威權，懼榮害之，復相間構，日月滋甚，於是莊帝密有圖榮之意。

translations.literal: Moreover Prince of Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Li Yu, and others wished to monopolize prestige and power. Fearing that Rong would harm them, they again sowed discord between the two sides. Day by day it grew worse, and so Emperor Zhuang secretly conceived the intention of plotting against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Hui, Palace Attendant Li Yu, and others sought power for themselves and feared Rong would destroy them. They fanned discord between emperor and general until, day by day, the breach widened — and Emperor Zhuang secretly resolved to destroy Rong.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，榮啟將入朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year, Rong memorialized that he would enter court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year Rong announced he would enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝士慮其有變，莊帝又畏惡之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen feared he would bring trouble; Emperor Zhuang also dreaded and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials feared trouble; Emperor Zhuang dreaded and hated him.

sentences.zh: 榮從弟世隆與榮書，勸其不來，榮妻北鄉郡長公主亦勸不行，榮並不從。

translations.literal: Rong's cousin Shilong wrote to Rong urging him not to come. Rong's wife, the Princess of Beixiang Commandery, also urged him not to go. Rong would not listen to either.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's cousin Shilong wrote urging him to stay away. Rong's wife, Princess of Beixiang Commandery, pleaded the same. Rong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝既圖榮，榮至入見，即欲害之，以天穆在并，恐為後患，故隱忍未發。

translations.literal: The emperor, having already plotted against Rong, wished to kill him as soon as Rong arrived and entered audience, but because Tianmu was in Bing Province he feared later trouble and therefore restrained himself and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already meant to kill Rong and would have done so at their first audience, but Tianmu still held Bing Province and might become a threat afterward — so he held back.

sentences.zh: 榮之入洛，有人告榮，云帝欲圖之。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, someone informed Rong that the emperor intended to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang someone warned him that the emperor meant to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 榮即具奏，帝曰：「外人告云亦言王欲害我，我豈信之？」

translations.literal: Rong immediately submitted a full report. The emperor said: "Outsiders also report that you, Prince, wish to harm me — how could I believe that?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong reported this at once. The emperor said, "Outsiders also say you mean to harm me — would I believe that?

sentences.zh: 於是榮不自疑，每入謁帝，從人不過數十，又皆挺身不持兵仗。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rong did not suspect himself. Each time he entered to attend upon the emperor, his followers numbered no more than several dozen, and all stood upright without carrying weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Rong took him at his word. Each time he attended the emperor he brought no more than a few dozen followers, all unarmed and standing at ease.

sentences.zh: 及天穆至，帝伏兵於明光殿東廊，引榮及榮長子菩提、天穆等俱入。

translations.literal: When Tianmu arrived, the emperor hid troops in the eastern corridor of Mingguang Hall and summoned Rong, Rong's eldest son Bodhi, Tianmu, and the others to enter together.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianmu arrived the emperor hid troops in the eastern corridor of Mingguang Hall and summoned Rong, Rong's eldest son Bodhi, Tianmu, and the others inside.

sentences.zh: 坐定，光祿少卿魯安、典御李侃晞等抽刀而至，榮窘迫，起投御坐。

translations.literal: Once they were seated, Vice Director of the Imperial Household Lu An, Palace Attendant Li Kanxi, and others drew their blades and rushed forward. Rong, cornered, rose and threw himself against the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: They had barely sat down when Vice Director of the Imperial Household Lu An, Palace Attendant Li Kanxi, and others drew their blades and rushed in. Cornered, Rong lunged toward the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 帝先橫刀膝下，遂手刃之，安等亂斫，榮與天穆、菩提同時俱死。

translations.literal: The emperor had already laid a blade across his knees and thereupon personally struck him down. An and the others hacked wildly. Rong, Tianmu, and Bodhi all died at the same moment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already had a blade across his knees and drove it home himself. An and the others hacked wildly. Rong, Tianmu, and Bodhi died together.

sentences.zh: 榮時年三十八。

translations.literal: Rong was thirty-eight years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 於是內外喜叫，聲滿京城。

translations.literal: Thereupon inside and outside rejoiced and shouted; the sound filled the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the palace cheers erupted until the capital rang with them.

sentences.zh: 既而大赦。

translations.literal: Soon afterward a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，世隆等得志，乃詔曰：「故使持節、侍中、都督河北諸軍事、天柱大將軍、大丞相、太師、領左右、兼錄尚書、北道大行臺、太原王榮，功濟區夏，誠貫幽明，天不憗遺，奄從物化。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of the Former Deposed Emperor, when Shilong and the others had their way, an edict said: "The late Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander of All Military Affairs in Hebei, Heaven-Pillar Grand General, Grand Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Commander of the Left and Right Guard, Concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Northern Route Grand Commissioner, Prince of Taiyuan, Rong — his achievement succored the Central Plain, his sincerity pierced the dark and the bright. Heaven did not long preserve him; suddenly he followed the transformation of things.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, when Shilong and his faction held power, an edict declared: "The late Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander of All Military Affairs in Hebei, Heaven-Pillar Grand General, Grand Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, Commander of the Left and Right Guard, Concurrent Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Northern Route Grand Commissioner, Prince of Taiyuan Rong — his achievement succored the Central Plain, his loyalty reached from this world to the next. Heaven did not long preserve him; suddenly he was gone.

sentences.zh: 追終褒績，列代通謨；

translations.literal: Posthumous honors and final praise of achievement — every age has shared this principle;
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors for the dead are the shared principle of every age;

sentences.zh: 紀德銘勳，前王令範。

translations.literal: recording virtue and inscribing merit — the worthy model of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: recording virtue and inscribing merit — the worthy model of kings past.

sentences.zh: 可贈假黃鉞、相國、錄尚書事、司州牧，使持節、侍中、將軍、王如故。」

translations.literal: Grant posthumously the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Chancellorship, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Governorship of Sizhou; Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, General, and Prince — all as before."
translations.idiomatic: Grant posthumously the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, the Chancellorship, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Governorship of Sizhou, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, General, and Prince — all as before.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「故假黃鉞、持節、侍中、相國、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事、天柱大將軍、司州牧、太原王榮，惟岳降靈，應期作輔，功侔伊霍，德契桓文。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The late holder of the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Heaven-Pillar Grand General, Governor of Sizhou, Prince of Taiyuan, Rong — a numinous spirit descended from the lofty peak, responding to the age as a supporting minister; achievement comparable to Yi and Huo, virtue in accord with Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: "The late holder of the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Heaven-Pillar Grand General, Governor of Sizhou, Prince of Taiyuan Rong — a numinous spirit descended from the sacred peak, called by the age to serve as pillar of state; merit comparable to Yi Yin and Huo Guang, virtue in the mold of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 方籍棟梁，永康國命，道長運短，震悼兼深。

translations.literal: Just as we relied on him as a pillar and beam to forever secure the fate of the state, the Way was long but his fortune was short — shock and grief together run deep.
translations.idiomatic: We had just leaned on him as the state's pillar to secure its future — yet the Way was long and his span was short. Shock and grief run deep together.

sentences.zh: 前已褒贈，用彰厥美。

translations.literal: Previously honors and gifts were already conferred to display his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Honors were already conferred to proclaim his excellence.

sentences.zh: 然禮數弗窮，文物有闕，遠近之望，猶或未盡。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual honors are not exhausted; ceremonial regalia still lacks. The hopes of far and near perhaps are not yet fully met.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual honors were not complete, ceremonial regalia still lacked, and the hopes of near and far were not yet fully satisfied.

sentences.zh: 宜循舊典，更加殊錫。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the old statutes and add further special bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Let ancient precedent be followed and further special honors added.

sentences.zh: 可追號為晉王，加九錫，給九旒鑾輅、虎賁、班劍三百人、轀輬車，準晉太宰、安平獻王故事，諡曰武。」

translations.literal: Posthumously grant the title Prince of Jin, add the Nine Bestowals, grant the nine-tassel imperial carriage, tiger guards, three hundred men with ceremonial swords, and the funeral carriage — following the precedent of the Grand Preceptor and Prince Xian of Anping of Jin. Posthumous title: Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously grant the title Prince of Jin with the Nine Bestowals — the nine-tassel imperial carriage, tiger guards, three hundred ceremonial sword-bearers, and the funeral carriage — following the precedent of Jin's Grand Preceptor, Prince Xian of Anping. Posthumous title: Wu."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「武泰之末，乾樞中圮，丕基寶命，有若綴旒。

translations.literal: An edict said: "At the end of the Wutai era, the imperial axis collapsed at its center; the great foundation and precious mandate hung like dangling tassels on a crown.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict declared: "At the close of the Wutai reign, the axis of heaven crumbled at its heart; the dynasty's great foundation and sacred mandate hung by a thread, like tassels dangling from a crown.

sentences.zh: 晉王榮固天所縱，世秉忠誠，一匡邦國，再造區夏，俾我頹綱，於斯復振。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Rong was indeed unleashed by Heaven; for generations he upheld loyalty and devotion, once set the state aright, twice restored the Central Realm, and caused our collapsing order to be restored at this time.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Rong was truly Heaven's chosen instrument — ever loyal through the generations. He set the kingdom aright once and restored the Central Realm anew, raising our fallen order from ruin.

sentences.zh: 雖勳銘王府，德被管絃，而從祀之禮，於茲尚闕，非所以酬懋賞於當時，騰殊績於不朽。

translations.literal: Although his merit is inscribed in the royal treasury and his virtue spreads to the pipes and strings, the rite of accompanying sacrifice is still lacking here — this is not how to reward splendid merit in its own time and elevate extraordinary achievement to immortality.
translations.idiomatic: Though his deeds are recorded in the royal annals and his virtue celebrated in song, the rite of joint sacrifice at the ancestral temple has yet to be granted — hardly fitting reward for such merit in its day, or the means to enshrine so great an achievement for all time.

sentences.zh: 宜遵舊典，配享高祖廟庭。」

translations.literal: He should follow the old rites and share sacrifice in the hall of the High Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Let the ancient precedent be observed: he shall receive joint sacrifice in the hall of Emperor Gaozu."

sentences.zh: 菩提，肅宗末，拜羽林監。

translations.literal: Puti, at the end of Emperor Suzong's reign, was appointed Director of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Puti, in the closing years of Emperor Suzong's reign, was appointed Director of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋轉直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the post of General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，以榮翼戴之勳，超授散騎常侍、平北將軍、中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, for Rong's merit in supporting and enthroning the emperor, he was specially appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang first took the throne, Puti was promoted above his rank to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the North, and Director of the Secretariat — reward for Zhurong's role in placing the emperor on the throne.

sentences.zh: 轉太常卿，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中、特進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Ceremonial, promoted to Rapid Cavalry Grand General and Opener of an Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Lords, with added titles of Palace Attendant and Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Ceremonial, then to Rapid Cavalry Grand General with an office equal in honor to the Three Highest Ministers, and was further granted the titles of Palace Attendant and Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 死時年十四。

translations.literal: When he died, he was fourteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fourteen.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，贈侍中、驃騎大將軍、司徒公、冀州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, he was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Jizhou. Posthumous title: Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor came to power, Puti was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Duke of the Ministry of Education, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 菩提弟叉羅，孝莊初，除散騎常侍、武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Puti's younger brother Chaluo, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Puti's younger brother Chaluo, at the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 初襲梁郡公，又進爵為王。

translations.literal: Initially he inherited the title Duke of Liang Commandery; then his ennoblement was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: He first inherited the title Duke of Liang Commandery, then was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈侍中、車騎將軍、司空公、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He soon died and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Chariot-and-Cavalry General, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant, Chariot-and-Cavalry General, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 文殊弟文暢，初封昌樂郡開國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Wenshu's younger brother Wenchang was initially enfeoffed as Duke of Chang Le Commandery with a founding state, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu's younger brother Wenchang was first enfeoffed as founding Duke of Chang Le Commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以榮破葛賊之勳，進爵為王，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: For Rong's merit in defeating Ge Rong's rebels, his ennoblement was advanced to prince and his fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhurong's victory over Ge Rong's bandits, Wenchang was raised to princely rank and his fief enlarged by a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 超授散騎常侍、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted above rank to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 後除肆州刺史，仍本將軍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Sizhou, retaining his rank as general, with the added title of Opener of an Office with Protocol Equal to the Three Lords.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Sizhou while retaining his military rank, and was further granted an office equal in honor to the Three Highest Ministers.

sentences.zh: 武定三年春，坐與前東郡太守任冑等謀反，[8]伏誅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Wuding, for plotting rebellion with the former Administrator of Dong Commandery Ren Zhou and others, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wuding 3, he was executed for conspiring to rebel with the former Administrator of Dong Commandery, Ren Zhou, and others.

sentences.zh: 時年十八。

translations.literal: At the time he was eighteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighteen at the time of his death.

sentences.zh: 文暢弟文略，襲爵梁郡王。

translations.literal: Wenchang's younger brother Wenlue inherited the title Prince of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang's younger brother Wenlue inherited the title of Prince of Liang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 武定末，撫軍將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, he held the posts of General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Wuding era, he served as General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太祖撫運乘時，奄開王業。

translations.literal: The historian says: Taizu seized the turning point of destiny and suddenly opened the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Taizu seized the momentum of the age and swiftly founded the royal line.

sentences.zh: 世祖以武功一海內，高祖以文德革天下。

translations.literal: Shizu united the realm within the four seas through military achievement; Gaozu transformed all under heaven through civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu brought the realm under one rule by force of arms; Emperor Gaozu remade the world through civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 世宗之後，政道頗虧。

translations.literal: After Shizong, the way of governance declined considerably.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizong's reign, good governance fell into steep decline.

sentences.zh: 及明皇幼沖，女主南面。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was young and tender, the female ruler faced south.
translations.idiomatic: When the young Emperor Ming came to the throne, the Empress Dowager held court as regent.

sentences.zh: 始則于忠專恣，繼以元叉權重，握賞罰之柄，擅生殺之威，榮悴在親疏，貴賤由離合，附會者結之以子女，進趨者要之以金帛。

translations.literal: At first Yu Zhong monopolized power at will; then Yuan Cha wielded heavy authority — grasping the handle of rewards and punishments, arrogating the power of life and death. Glory and ruin depended on closeness or distance; noble and base were determined by alliance or estrangement. Those who attached themselves were bound by marriage of sons and daughters; those who sought advancement were secured with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: First Yu Zhong ruled unchecked; then Yuan Cha amassed overwhelming power — controlling rewards and punishments, wielding the authority of life and death. Favor and ruin hinged on whether one stood near or far; rank rose or fell with allegiance or defection. Supporters were bound by offers of marriage; climbers were bought with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 且佞諛用事，功勤不賞，居官肆其聚斂，乘勢極其陵暴。

translations.literal: Moreover, flatterers and sycophants held office; merit and hard service went unrewarded. Officials in office indulged in extortionate gathering of wealth, and those who rode the tide of power carried oppression to its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers held sway, and loyal service went unrewarded. Officials plundered without restraint, and the powerful abused their position to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 於是四海囂然，已有羣飛之漸矣。

translations.literal: Thus the four seas grew clamorous, and there were already signs of flocking disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The realm grew restless, and the first stirrings of mass upheaval were already visible.

sentences.zh: 逮於靈后反政，宣淫於朝。

translations.literal: When Empress Ling resumed governance, she spread licentiousness at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Ling regained power, she flaunted her debauchery throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼手運天機，口吐王制。

translations.literal: Zheng Yan manipulated heaven's secrets with his hands and issued royal edicts from his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yan commanded the levers of state from his fingertips and issued imperial decrees from his lips.

sentences.zh: 李軌、徐紇刺促以求先，元略、元徽喔咿以競入。

translations.literal: Li Gui and Xu He scurried in haste to get ahead; Yuan Lue and Yuan Hui fawned and whined to compete for entry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui and Xu He scrambled to push ahead of the rest; Yuan Lue and Yuan Hui wheedled their way into favor.

sentences.zh: 私利畢舉，公道盡亡，遐邇怨憤，天下鼎沸。

translations.literal: Private profit was fully pursued; public justice was wholly lost. Near and far resented and raged; all under heaven seethed like a boiling cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Private greed ran its course until public justice was extinguished; resentment flared from every corner, and the empire boiled over.

sentences.zh: 傾覆之徵，於此至矣。

translations.literal: The signs of overturning and collapse had at this point reached their limit.
translations.idiomatic: By then the portents of ruin had reached their full measure.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮緣將帥之列，藉部眾之用，屬肅宗暴崩，民怨神怒，遂有匡頹拯弊之志，援主逐惡之圖，蓋天啟之也。

translations.literal: Er Zhurong arose from the ranks of generals and borrowed the use of his troops and followers. When Emperor Suzong suddenly died, the people resented and the spirits raged — thus he had the ambition to right the tottering and save the failing, and the design to support the sovereign and drive out the wicked. Perhaps Heaven opened the way.
translations.idiomatic: Er Zhurong rose from the ranks of military commanders, drawing on the strength of his tribal forces. When Emperor Suzong died suddenly amid widespread outrage, Zhurong conceived the ambition to rescue a collapsing state and restore a broken order — to uphold the rightful ruler and purge the wicked. Perhaps Heaven itself opened the way.

sentences.zh: 於時，上下離心，文武解體，咸企忠義之聲，俱聽桓文之舉。

translations.literal: At that time, those above and below were disunited in heart; civil and military ranks disintegrated. All looked to voices of loyalty and righteousness; all listened for actions like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country had lost all cohesion; civil officials and military men alike had come apart. Everyone awaited a voice of loyalty and righteousness; everyone listened for a Huan or Wen of the age.

sentences.zh: 勞不汗馬，朝野靡然，扶翼懿親，宗祏有主，祀魏配天，不殞舊物。

translations.literal: Labor without sweating horses — court and countryside were utterly transformed. He supported and enthroned the worthy kinsman; the ancestral tablet had its lord. Wei was worshipped and matched with Heaven; the old inheritance was not lost.
translations.idiomatic: Without the weary toll of prolonged campaigning, court and countryside fell into line. He enthroned the worthy imperial kinsman; the ancestral altars had their rightful keeper once more. Wei continued to be worshipped alongside Heaven, and the dynasty's ancient patrimony endured.

sentences.zh: 及夫擒葛榮，誅元顥，戮邢杲，翦韓婁，醜奴、寶夤咸梟馬市。

translations.literal: As for capturing Ge Rong, executing Yuan Hao, killing Xing Gao, cutting down Han Lou — Chou Nu and Bao Yin were all exposed at Horse Market.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Ge Rong, executed Yuan Hao, killed Xing Gao, and destroyed Han Lou; Chou Nu and Bao Yin were all put to death and their heads displayed at Horse Market.

sentences.zh: 此諸魁者，或據象魏，或僭號令，人謂秉皇符，身各謀帝業，非徒鼠竊狗盜，一城一聚而已。

translations.literal: These chieftains either held the Elephant Gate or usurped imperial titles and commands; people said they held the royal talisman, each personally scheming for the imperial enterprise — not merely rats stealing and dogs plundering, limited to one city or one gathering.
translations.idiomatic: These rebel leaders had seized the imperial capital or proclaimed themselves sovereign; each claimed heaven's mandate and plotted for the throne. They were far more than mere bandits raiding a town or a cluster of villages.

sentences.zh: 苟非榮之致力，克夷大難，則不知幾人稱帝，幾人稱王也。

translations.literal: If Rong had not exerted himself to pacify the great calamity, then one would not know how many would have called themselves emperor, how many would have called themselves king.
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhurong not thrown himself into quelling the catastrophe, who can say how many men would have proclaimed themselves emperor — or king?

sentences.zh: 然則榮之功烈，亦已茂乎。

translations.literal: Thus Rong's achievements and merit were indeed abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements, then, were truly great.

sentences.zh: 而始則希覬非望，睥睨宸極；

translations.literal: Yet at the beginning he coveted improper ambition and looked askance at the imperial throne;
translations.idiomatic: Yet at first he harbored illicit ambition and cast his eyes toward the throne;

sentences.zh: 終乃靈后、少帝沉流不反。

translations.literal: In the end, Empress Ling and the young emperor were drowned in the river and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: and in the end Empress Ling and the young emperor were cast into the river, never to return.

sentences.zh: 河陰之下，衣冠塗地。

translations.literal: Below Heyin, the gentry were strewn across the ground.
translations.idiomatic: At the slaughter by the Yellow River at Heyin, the scholar-official class was mowed down by the thousands.

sentences.zh: 此其所以得罪人神，而終於夷戮也。

translations.literal: This is why he offended both men and gods and ultimately ended in execution and annihilation.
translations.idiomatic: This is why he earned the condemnation of gods and men alike, and met his end in ruin and death.

sentences.zh: 向使榮無姦忍之失，修德義之風，則彭、韋、伊、霍夫何足數。

translations.literal: If Rong had not had the faults of wickedness and cruelty and had cultivated the spirit of virtue and righteousness, then Peng, Wei, Yi, and Huo would scarcely be worth counting against him.
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhurong lacked his cruelty and treachery and instead cultivated virtue and righteousness, even the great restorers Peng, Wei, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang would have paled beside him.

sentences.zh: 至於末迹見猜，地逼貽斃，斯則蒯通致說於韓王也。

translations.literal: As for his final career being suspected and his proximity to power causing his death — this was like Kuai Tong presenting his argument to the King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: As for his final years — feared for his ambition, destroyed because power lay too close at hand — his fate resembled that of Kuai Tong advising the King of Han.

translations.idiomatic: "The governor of Southern Xiurong's son Wanzi Qizhen rebelled" — in juan 9 of the Annals of Emperor Suzong, under the dingyou day of the eighth month, Zhengguang 5, "Wanzi Qizhen" appears as "Yu Qizhen."

translations.idiomatic: Examining juan 113, Treatise on Clans, "The Wunüyu clan later changed to the Yu clan." Guangyun, fascicle 10 Yu, citing the Wei Chronicles, writes "Wu" as "Wan."

translations.idiomatic: "Attached rebel barbarians Qibuluo Jian Hu Liu Aru and others rose in rebellion at Gua-Si" — the character qi suggests missing text above or below it, leaving the personal names incomplete.

translations.idiomatic: "Gua" is likely a scribal error for "Fen" [i.e., Fenzhou].

translations.literal: "Chile tribesman Beilie Buro rebelled at Woyang" — examining: this book juan 80 has the Chilie Yanqing biography; Zhou shu juan 20 has Chilie Fugui biography; Bei Qi shu juan 20 has Chilie Ping biography — all say people of the Western Dai region.
translations.idiomatic: "The Chile chieftain Beilie Buro rebelled at Woyang" — compare juan 80 of this work (Biography of Chilie Yanqing), juan 20 of the Zhou History (Biography of Chilie Fugui), and juan 20 of the Northern Qi History (Biography of Chilie Ping); all identify the clan as from western Dai.

sentences.zh: 叱列平字殺鬼，北史卷四八稱他為「西部高車叱列殺鬼」。

translations.literal: Chilie Ping, courtesy name Shagui — Beishi juan 48 calls him "Western-region Gaoche Chilie Shagui."
translations.idiomatic: Chilie Ping, styled Shagui — juan 48 of the History of the North calls him "Chilie Shagui of the western Gaoche."

sentences.zh: 高車即敕勒，叱列是敕勒姓，這裏「北列」乃「叱列」之訛。

translations.literal: Gaoche is Chile; Chilie is a Chile surname — here "Beilie" is a corruption of "Chilie."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche is another name for the Chile; Chilie is a Chile clan name. Here "Beilie" is a scribal error for "Chilie."

sentences.zh: 敕勒斛律洛陽作逆桑乾西 諸本「斛」作「解」，卷九肅宗紀孝昌二年三月甲寅條作「斛」。

translations.literal: "The Chile chieftain Hulü Luoyang rebelled west of Sanggan" — in various editions "Hu" is written "Jie"; juan 9 Suzong annals, third month, jiayin day, second year of Xiaochang writes "Hu."
translations.idiomatic: "The Chile chieftain Hulü Luoyang rebelled west of the Sanggan River" — several editions read jie for hu; juan 9 of the Suzong annals, under jiayin of the third month, Xiaochang 2, has hu.

sentences.zh: 按斛律是敕勒有名的部落，見卷一０三高車傳

translations.literal: Examining: Hulü is a famous Chile tribe — see juan 103, Gaoche biography
translations.idiomatic: The Hulü were a well-known Chile tribe — see juan 103, Biography of the Gaoche

translations.idiomatic: 〈Text supplied by the editor.〉

translations.idiomatic: , and juan 17 of the Northern Qi History, Biography of Hulü Jin.

translations.literal: "Jie" is a graphic corruption of "Hu"; now amended according to the basic annals.
translations.idiomatic: "Jie" is a graphic error for "Hu"; amended here according to the annals.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史李神軌閉門自守 北史卷四八「神軌」作「神儁」。

translations.literal: "Governor of Xiangzhou Li Shengui shut the gates and held self-defense" — Beishi juan 48 writes "Shengui" as "Shenjun."
translations.idiomatic: "Governor of Xiangzhou Li Shengui shut the gates and held the city" — juan 48 of the History of the North reads Shenjun for Shengui.

sentences.zh: 張矰讀史舉正云：「按神軌死於河陰之難，贈相州刺史，見本書列傳

translations.literal: Zhang Zheng's Reading History with Corrections states: "Examining: Shengui died in the Heyin catastrophe; he was posthumously granted Governor of Xiangzhou — see this book's biographical section
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zheng's Critical Notes on Reading History observes: "Shengui died in the Heyin massacre and was posthumously named Governor of Xiangzhou — see the biographical section of this work

sentences.zh: 〈卷六六〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 66〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 66〉

sentences.zh: ，河陰事在此先，傳亦不言其曾為相州刺史，當由贈相州刺史致誤耳。

translations.literal: ; the Heyin affair came before this, and the biography also does not say he ever served as Governor of Xiangzhou — it must be an error caused by the posthumous grant of Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ; the Heyin incident predates this passage, and his biography nowhere says he actually served as governor — the error likely arose from his posthumous appointment to that office.

sentences.zh: 考神儁傳

translations.literal: Examining Shenjun's biography
translations.idiomatic: Examining the biography of Shenjun

translations.literal: 〈juan 39〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 39〉

sentences.zh: ，肅宗末，行相州事。

translations.literal: , at the end of Suzong's reign, administered Xiangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: , at the close of Emperor Suzong's reign he administered Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮南逼，神儁憂懼，故墜馬傷脚，仍停汲郡，有詔追還。

translations.literal: At the time Ge Rong pressed south; Shenjun was anxious and fearful, hence fell from his horse and injured his foot. He still halted at Ji Commandery, and there was an edict summoning him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong drove south, Shenjun grew fearful, fell from his horse and injured his foot, and remained at Ji Commandery until recalled by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 莊帝纂統，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Shenjun was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 據此，神儁刺相州，在孝莊即位之先，且身未至相州，安得有『閉門自守』之事。

translations.literal: According to this, Shenjun's appointment to Xiangzhou was before Emperor Xiaozhuang's enthronement, and moreover he himself never reached Xiangzhou — how could there be the affair of "shutting the gates and holding self-defense"?
translations.idiomatic: On this evidence, Shenjun's commission to Xiangzhou predated Emperor Xiaozhuang's accession, and he never actually reached the province — how then could he have "shut the gates and held the city"?

sentences.zh: 而本書李神傳

translations.literal: Yet this book's Li Shen biography
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Biography of Li Shen in this work

sentences.zh: 〈卷七０〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 70〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 70〉

sentences.zh: 云：孝昌中，行相州事。

translations.literal: states: In the Xiaochang era, he administered Xiangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: records: during the Xiaochang era he administered Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建義初，葛榮盡銳攻之，久不能克。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Ge Rong attacked with all his elite forces for a long time but could not overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era, Ge Rong assaulted the city with his full strength but failed to take it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 會尒朱榮擒葛榮，事平，以功進爵。

translations.literal: When Er Zhurong captured Ge Rong and the affair was settled, he advanced in ennoblement for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Er Zhurong captured Ge Rong and the crisis ended, Li Shen was ennobled for his service.

sentences.zh: 然則李神及神軌、神儁姓名略同，事又並在一時前後，必有乖錯。

translations.literal: Thus Li Shen and Shengui and Shenjun have slightly similar names; their affairs also all occurred in the same period before and after — there must be confusion and error.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, Shengui, and Shenjun have similar names, and their careers all fall in the same period — some confusion is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 獨神傳有『久不能克』等語，與『閉門自守』之文頗合，疑當是李神也。」

translations.literal: Only Shen's biography has the words "for a long time could not overcome it" and the like, which rather fits the text "shut the gates and hold self-defense" — it is suspected it ought to be Li Shen."
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Shen's biography mentions that Ge Rong "could not overcome it for a long time" — language that fits "shutting the gates and holding the city." The reference is probably to Li Shen."

sentences.zh: 按卷六八甄琛傳附見張宣軌，亦記李神守相州事，張說是。

translations.literal: Examining juan 68 Zhen Chen biography's appended mention of Zhang Xuangui, which also records Li Shen's defense of Xiangzhou — Zhang's account is correct.
translations.idiomatic: See also the appended mention of Zhang Xuangui in juan 68 (Biography of Zhen Chen), which likewise records Li Shen's defense of Xiangzhou. Zhang's account is correct.

sentences.zh: 魏收是同時人，未必乖誤至此，原文當是「李神」，「軌」「儁」或是後人妄加。

translations.literal: Wei Shou was a contemporary — he need not have erred to this degree. The original text ought to be "Li Shen"; "Gui" and "Jun" were perhaps added falsely by later hands.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was a contemporary eyewitness and unlikely to have erred so badly. The original reading was probably "Li Shen"; "Gui" and "Jun" may have been inserted by later copyists.

translations.idiomatic: "Divine" (shen) appears as "sleeve" (xiu); "sleeve" is probably the correct reading.
